GTNH is divided up into tiers. Each new tier unlocks more materials, machines, multiblocks and mods available to use. The first ten tiers up to UHV are considered fully implemented, while major changes are still in development for UEV-MAX. Tier is a common term used by many mods, to represent the player's level of progress of any sort; other tiered mechanics are listed below.

documents.text:
Low Voltage (LV) is the first electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. With access to electricity comes new hazards and mechanics, but also far more variety of specialized machines that can process materials into new parts with greater efficiency.
Goals
Some of the primary milestones for this tier are as follows:
- Batch craft Electronic Circuits
- LV components - Motor, Piston, Pump, Robot Arm, Sensor, Emitter
- LV Machines - Bending Machine (priority), Wiremill (priority), Lathe, Assembler, Electrolyzer, Chemical Reactor, Fluid Extractor, etc.
- Acquire Lithium and Lead for Batteries
- Pump Oil for Polyethylene and Light Fuel
- Upgrade Power Generation
- Build Good Circuits
- Locate Mica (or make the more expensive Alumino Silicate Wool)
- Construct an Electric Blast Furnace & maintenance tools to get Aluminum
Optional Side Quests:
- Increase Hearts by eating a variety of foods
- Plan for a larger base to accommodate MV machines / multiblocks
- Make multiple Backpacks (Forestry/ModdedNetwork)
- Hang Glider , Piston Boots , Healing Axe (if not already acquired)
- Visit the Twilight Forest
- More storage with drawer/barrel upgrades, Diamond Chests
- Sound Mufflers, Chandeliers
- Tool & Armor Upgrades
- Item Dislocator (or another Magnet )
EU (Energy Units) Mechanics
GregTech energy consists of Voltage and Amperage. A Low Voltage (LV) GT generator will output 32 volts (32V) in 1 amperage (1A/1 amp). Four generators on the same cable will output 32 volts in 4 amps combined. 32 volts in 4 amps is not the same thing as MV (Medium Voltage - 128 volts per amp). This can be compared to four cables containing 32 volts each, or one 4x Cable. The x rating of a cable (x1, x2, x4, etc.) denotes its maximum amperage. The general rule of thumb is your cables should have an equal Amp capacity to the number of generators/batteries attached. Battery Buffers output 1A per battery , while virtually every generator puts out 1A. Having a cable with enough Amperage capacity for all of them at once prevents fires and explosions .
For more advanced and complete information, see Electricity .
Energy Loss
The tooltip for GT cables show their max voltage, max Amperage and Loss per Meter/Ampere. A cable or wire will catch fire if it receives more than its max voltage or max amperage. A normal 1x Tin Cable will lose 1 volt for each block (meter) length of the cable. Uncoated wires lose even more per block and present a shock hazard, so never use bare wire to connect machines. If the distance between the power input and machine is 10 blocks long, and the generator is generating 32 volts in 1 amp, then there will only be 22 volts in 1 amp remaining on the other end of the cable. With a LV battery buffer with 4 LV batteries inside, it would send 32 volts in up to 4 amps, but after 10 blocks there will only be 22 volts each amp remaining. Lossless cables are gated behind Redstone Alloy and the Electric Blast Furnace , so until available players are well advised to keep cables as short as possible.
Battery Buffers
Battery Buffers are used to store EU Energy, at a 5% loss cost. Battery Buffers can be made in variable capacities between 1x and 16x internal slots. The Buffer itself does not store power; batteries matching the tier have to be inserted into the Battery Buffer to make it function. Each battery added will increase the buffer's capacity by +2 amps input and +1 amp output. Since buffers can have a variable amperage output based on the number of inserted batteries, care must be taken to ensure the cable has sufficient capacity to handle the buffer's maximum output. This becomes more relevant when multiple machines are all requesting amps at the same time over a longer cable.
GT Electric Machines
Machine GUI. Auto-output buttons circled in yellow.
LV Electric machines have some new features that were not available with Steam-age machinery. For example, the steam exhaust is replaced with an automatic output. This output's facing can be changed with a wrench similar to how the exhaust was configured on Steam machines. Just like their Steam counterparts, all electric GT machines cannot be input or output from their front face. To enable automatic output, open the GUI of the machine and click on the button at the lower left corner. There are two automatic output toggle buttons; the left one is for liquid and the right one is for items.
Electrolyzer clay dust recipe. The MV power requirement is circled in yellow.
GregTech machinery is divided by tier, which corresponds to a specific voltage - LV (32 V), MV (128 V), HV (512 V) etc. Most recipes are gated to a specific voltage/tier or higher, which is shown with the recipe in NEI (Not Enough Items). If the recipe requires more than one amp it will also be listed here. Pay careful attention to what tier a recipe requires - with LV machinery, MV and higher recipes are inaccessible.
For example, putting Clay Dust through the Electrolyzer to get Aluminium dust requires 120 EU/t (MV). Since the Basic Electrolyzer is only able to do 32EU/t, this recipe is unavailable until the Advanced Electrolyzer (MV).
Recipes close to the voltage limit for LV (32 EU/t) may cause the machine to request multiple amps, especially if there is any cable loss. A single LV generator will often not be capable of supplying enough power if the machine is placed too far away. Most GT machines will accept up to 2 amps. A second generator or Battery Buffer may be needed to keep a a high cost recipe running. If a machine runs out of power, it will stall resetting any progress but not losing the materials. A soft mallet can be used to temporarily disable a machine to give a buffer time to recharge or wait until more power generation is available.
Some machines require multiple amps to run at all, such as the Arc Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace . The Arc Furnace requires 3 amps to function and can accept up to 7 amps. Checking any recipe for the Arc Furnace will show Usage XX/t, voltage 32 EU/t and amperage X. The Electric Blast Furnace is even more demanding, taking four amps of LV minimum for its most basic recipes.
Explosions
Machines, wires and cables can overload, resulting in fires and explosions .
Rain will make your electric machines explode if the rain is on any adjacent blocks to the machine, so put your machinery under a proper roof. Uninsulated wires will also catch on fire from rain. Fire adjacent to machines will cause them to explode, potentially taking out more machines and causing significant Pollution . Water does not cause fires/explosions; it's perfectly safe to have water blocks adjacent to machines.
Giving machines a higher voltage than they are rated for will make them explode. This won't become an issue before unlocking MV , but it's important enough to mention early and often. Excess Amperage on a cable is not an issue, as long as it doesn't exceed the cable's rating. Machines will only accept as many Amps as they need.
Energy Conversion
IC2 EU
To transform IC2 energy into GT energy you simply need to place a GT transformer or power storage next to the IC2 power source. Keep in mind that IC2 generation is typically only 1 amp, therefore the Transformer should be in Step-Down mode. GT cables/wires can be used to connect IC2 machines, but pay attention to the EU output. Some devices such as the Stirling Generator output more than 32EU, and thus require at least x2 cable.
GT EU to Others
GT Cables can be attached to almost any machine that requires some kind of energy, allowing a single power network to run machines from most mods in the pack including IC2, EnderIO, Forestry, Railcraft, Galacticraft and more. Due to the idiosyncrasies of ENet, at least one GT machine (a machine hull will do the job nicely) has to be present for power to transfer on GT cables/wires. Placing the cable last sometimes also helps the setup register as valid.
Revisiting Steam
The LV Age opens up full automation for Steam and new machines like the Assembler and Bender provide substantial discounts to crafting costs, especially for the Multiblocks.
Steam Power Upgrades
Up until LV your most automated options for generating Steam involved either regularly resetting Solar Boilers or collecting wood manually to feed Coke Ovens, the LV Crop Manager and tree bonsais allow for easy and cheap automation of Wood, enabling fully automatic power. Look into powering it with a semifluid generator directly with creosote, its a bit more power efficient and saves on pipe distance in most builds. You can try and breed the bonsais for max stats but that won't be necessary, even one 11x11 layer of 1/1/1 bonsais will provide more than enough wood for a max size RC Boiler . Speaking of RC boilers, the tank recipe gets substantially cheaper in LV, with the screw requirement being dropped with the assembler; the casing required for the tanks can also be made cheaper by utilising the Bender and the Cutting Machine.
After visiting the Twilight Forest, the player can utilise the lead found to make Potin fluid pipes, which offer substantially more throughput than Bronze pipes of the same size. You can utilise the Fluid Extractor and Solidifier to produce pipes substantially quicker than with the Bender.
Revisiting Multiblocks
Steam Multiblocks are made substantially cheaper in LV with the Bender and Assembler, most of these multiblocks are not superseded until HV or later so it is well worth the investment to build them. After unlocking the EBF, Steel production is trivialised and the player should consider upgrading Steam Multiblocks accordingly for a speed upgrade. If you are having issues getting enough oxygen, electrolysing Magnetite and Limonite ores should get the player through to MV.
Progression
Progression to MV requires the player to obtain 3 essential materials:
• Gallium -
There is no renewable way to obtain Gallium in LV. The best way is to electrolyze Sphalerite dust, giving an 11% chance for Gallium. Gallium is also obtainable as a byproduct of Zinc ore processing, Zinc Gravel can be purchased with Blacksmith coins at regular enough intervals that it shouldn't be a major issue for now. You can also use XP buckets if you're desperate. With an HV macerator you can obtain more byproducts from ore processing, making Gallium much easier to obtain.
• Arsenic -
Cobaltite is the primary way of obtaining Arsenic in LV. When Cobaltite is blasted in an EBF with oxygen it produces roasted cobalt and arsenic dust. Running roasted arsenic dust through the EBF again results in 3 arsenic ingots per 2 cobaltite. This process is oxygen neutral after electrolyzing the carbon dioxide produced.
• Aluminum -
Aluminum has 2 ways to be obtained in LV, one involves compressing Aluminum dust and blasting the "raw Aluminum" into 1 Aluminum ingot. This recipe is slow and not recommended. The other recipe uses 10 Alumina and 5 cryolite to produce 4 Aluminum ingots. While being more involved, this recipe offers much faster and more power efficient Aluminum.
New Materials
Many new materials are available in LV that were unrealistic or unobtainable in Steam. Most originate in the Twilight forest, a dimension unlocked in LV .
Resources | How to obtain
Resources: Lead, Silver, Cryolite | How to obtain: Twilight Forest ore vein
Thaumcraft shard ores
Resources: Oil | How to obtain: Small fluid pump
Resources: Redstone Alloy, Dark Steel, Vanadiumsteel etc. | How to obtain: Mixer alloying and EBF blasting

documents.text:
Medium Voltage (MV) is the second electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. It introduces fewer new mechanics, but instead improves and expands what the player has already seen in LV .
Goals
Some of the suggested milestones the player should look for in MV are:
- Craft the Electrolyzer to split many natural resources into basic elements, most notably aluminium, oxygen and silicon.
- Upgrade your LV machines - you probably can't pass by the Arc Furnace, Assembler, Circuit Assembler, Chemical Reactor, Chemical Bath, Cutting Machine, Extruder, Fluid Extractor, Fluid Solidifier and/or Laser Engraver.
- Diesel is a significant improvement over Light Fuel which can be mixed in the MV Mixer.
- Tree farm setups can switch from Steam to Benzene, but will require Gas Turbines.
- Make a silicon processing line and start accumulating solar grade silicon, you'll need it later.
- Making lots of Polyethylene is also a good idea, automating it is even better.
- Upgrade your EBF (s) with Kanthal coils to smelt new ingots.
- Find sources of Chrome and Manganese for stainless steel, a material used very heavily in HV.
Optional Side Quests
- Aluminium & defeating the first Twilight Forest boss Naga, which gives the player access to Thaumcraft .
- Create the Good Miner for additional mining range and fortune bonus. Remember that it can be powered by LV generators.
- Use EnderIO Item Conduits to instantly move things around complex networks. The EnderIO conduits have additional bonuses, such as routing, support for item filtering, and the ability to pull from non-output machine sides, but have less throughput without upgrades.
- Use the Tool Forge to fill out your set of Tinker's Construct Hammer/Excavator/Scythe/Cleaver and other tools.
- Convert single-block steam/LV machines to their MV counterparts, or upgrade to Steam multiblocks ( Steam Oven , Steam Grinder , Steam Squasher , etc).
- Start Bees or IC2 Crops for renewable resources.
- Botania & Witchery.
Explosions, Part Two
On top of the concerns from LV machinery, the addition of MV power means keeping higher voltage lines away from low voltage cables and machines. Giving machines a higher voltage than they are rated for will make them explode . Putting MV power on a LV cable/wire will make it burn up, catch fire and potentially explode adjacent machines. To avoid a catastrophic failure by accidental over-voltage, separate LV and MV machinery rooms, use different cable sizes, and/or paint your cables.
Providing a lower voltage than a machine is rated for is safe. For examples, while a Good Miner is MV-tier, it only uses 1/4 of an MV amp, meaning that as long as a there isn't any cable loss, it can be powered with 1A of LV energy.
Transformers
Transformer in default mode, tranforming 1A HV to 4A MV. The single dotted sides are MV outputs while the HV input is the bigger, hollow + circle on the left
Transformers are used to convert EU between power tiers . To run LV machinery off MV power generation, a Transformer is necessary to convert the energy into LV voltage. One Amp (1A) of the higher tier will make four Amps (4A) of the next tier down in Step-Down mode, the default (1A MV -> 4A LV). In Inverted Step-Up mode, Transformers can take four lower voltage amps and output a single higher voltage amp (4A LV -> 1A MV). Keep in mind that in this mode the lower voltage sides become the Input, and the higher voltage side is therefore the Output. The single larger circle on a Transformer is always the side that connects to the higher voltage.
Hit the transformer with a Soft Mallet to switch between its two modes. “Machine Active” is Step-Down mode, "Machine Inactive" is Step-Up mode. Never change mode on a transformer that has power or it will explode . Always disconnect cables before switching modes on Transformers.
Power Transformer
The Power Transformer works like an ordinary transformer with one exception. It will accept 4A of higher voltage and turn it into 16A of lower voltage in its default mode. In inverted mode it will transform 16A of lower voltage to 4A of higher voltage.
Materials
MV is a new tier, and will require new materials. The player should find a mesa biome in order to source clay dust for aluminum. A large amount of aluminum is used in MV, expect multiple trips to a mesa!
The player should stockpile multiple resources during early MV such as silicon dioxide/raw silicon and cryolite, which is used for aluminum production. Mining 3 Galena veins should provide enough for most of MV.
Raw silicon is used in mid/late MV to produce solar grade silicon. Solar grade silicon is used everywhere from HV-LuV. Expect to automate this (see automation section for more details).
Automation
Oxygen should be first to be automated. Breed some max stat sugar beet seeds and get a Crop Manager on it, that plus an electrolyser or two should carry you well past EV. Alternately, Sweed can be made with a little Thaumcraft progression and harvested with the Ender IO Farming Station.
Polyethylene is vital to progression to HV and should be automated as soon as possible. The main issue is obtaining ethylene. You can use multiple different machines to obtain ethylene.
• Pyrolyse oven - The Pyrolyse oven produces charcoal, but we are more interested in the byproducts. Wood gas can be used directly in a distillery to produce ethylene. Don't expect this to last, this setup is slow.
• Oil - Oil can be used to produce ethylene through a long line of processing: Oil ->(Distillery) sulfuric naphtha
Sulfuric naphtha ->(Chemical Reactor) Naphtha
Naphtha ->(Chemical Reactor) Severely steamcracked naphtha
Severely steamcracked naphtha ->(Distillery) Ethylene Note: other Oil products like refinery gas can be used, look at NEI for what best suits your setup.
• Biofuel - For completely renewable ethylene, consider biofuel. Consult NEI, there are many ways to do this.
Another material needed to be automated is solar grade silicon. There are two ways to do this, as listed in the quest book. Method one requires more machines but is faster overall than method 2. Most players go with method 2, as the time save isnt significant enough to matter.
Progression
There are 3 main goals in MV. 1. Obtaining Stainless Steel 2. Semi/Fully automatic Polyethylene 3. HV Circuits ("advanced circuit")
This section will cover all 3 in detail.
Every goal discussed here is gated behind an EBF with Kanthal coils and MV power.
1. Stainless steel is a very important material required for virtually everything in HV. The dust is made with a mix of chrome, manganese, iron and nickel (or invar, which is just a mix of the last two).
Nickel can be sourced from nickel ore in the twilight forest, or as byproduct of some basic ore processing chains (iron, gold, copper)
Chrome has multiple ways it can be sourced. Electrolyzing ruby dust provides some chrome, but it is instead recommended to use a ruby juice line (whether manually or automatically) to process ruby for much more chrome.
Manganese can be sourced from Grossular ore veins (one of the rarest veins in the game!) Or alternatively from XP buckets. It is recommended to use Grossular veins, as they also provide tantalum. Tantalum is used for SMD transistors and better SMD resistor recipes.
2. Automate various things. (see automation section)
3. HV circuits are the mark of the start of HV. They are very complicated and require a new circuit line: integrated circuits. They also require transistors, which is why solar grade silicon should be automated. (see automation section)
Integrated circuits will be new and not simple to craft! Its not a sign that your base isn't strong enough to handle HV if these circuits take a long time to craft/figure out.
Transistors require solar grade silicon, but if you have been electrolyzing clay for alumina that shouldn't be a problem. They will also take some time to figure out.
Don't expect HV to be easier. This game doesn't have a difficulty curve, it has a difficulty cliff.

documents.text:
High Voltage (HV) is the third electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, several new mechanics are introduced to you such as cleanrooms , space travel , and multiblock versions of your singleblock machines. With the introduction of the Cleanroom, your ability to produce more complex circuits and some of their critical components will be restricted to the inside of the Cleanroom multiblock structure, or other multiblocks that are also considered cleanrooms. Many important materials, such as titanium, can only be extracted from ores that exist on other planets and celestial bodies. You will find that all of these mechanics will carry on with you for the foreseeable future.
Upon reaching HV, you should either have the ability to produce large quantities of stainless steel or quickly plan on developing the infrastructure to do so, as this is the first tier that starts demanding large quantities of its respective machine hull material, whether it's through the numerous single block machines or new multi-block machines such as the expensive but rewarding Distillation Tower.
Progression
The Start / Early-HV
You should start making HV generators for this energy tier, as well as the HV Chemical Reactor and Mixer. After making the machines listed, you should focus on the MV Circuit Assembler, as it is the next step in creating the Cleanroom. The completion of the Cleanroom should be one of your priorities, as it significantly reduces the costs of your circuits, and is a required stepping stone to progress! You are gated from the Distillation Tower and NASA workbench until your Cleanroom is up and running.
First Energy Crisis
You may find yourself struggling to power HV EBFs and possibly even your singleblock machines for long periods of time, as each HV machine you make consumes 4x (not accounting for efficiency loss) the amount of fuel compared to your MV generators. You should expand and fully automate your energy production setup.
In HV, combustion generators gain a massive buff thanks to the addition of Cetane-Boosted Diesel, which boasts a whopping 1M EU per cell, a massive expansion over Diesel. In addition, Benzene is heavily improved thanks to the Distillation Tower and Pyrolyse Oven coil upgrades which significantly speed up Benzene production. The Distillation Tower will even produce Phenol and Toluene which can be burned in Gas Turbines if you're in a pinch. Note that these infrastructure upgrades require significant amounts of resources upfront, but the infrastructure investment easily carries over into EV.
Mid-HV
With a more powerful energy infrastructure setup and running Cleanroom, you can start working on EV circuits, perfect for creating the HV Circuit Assembler. The HV Circuit Assembler allows you to make IV circuits, which are necessary for the NASA Workbench. From now on, your copper consumption will greatly increase due to the massive demand from plastic circuit boards.
You will also want to look at the new multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor, Distillation Tower, Oil Cracker, and Vacuum Freezer.
The Large Chemical Reactor might not be absolutely mandatory yet, but has some huge benefits: it has perfect overclocks, meaning that speed will quadruple every tier with ZERO additional power cost, it allows you to stop using cells for liquids, and it gates many extremely useful recipes such as a two-step PTFE recipe (for more LCRs) and one-step sulfuric acid from sulfur. The Distillation Tower will be your most expensive multiblock (requiring about ~56 Stainless Steel ingots for every layer), but the added efficiency in both resource production and energy consumption will make it absolutely worth it in the long run.
The Vacuum Freezer is not absolutely necessary until whenever you need Nichrome coils, but is worth crafting sooner than later. It is much cheaper to craft than you might expect (hopefully you have at least 2 and a half stacks of aluminium laying around at this point?) and massively reduces time and energy consumption for whatever Hot Ingots you may have originally been cooling using the Chemical Bath.
The Multi Smelter looks similar to an EBF but requires half the coils. It has insanely good efficiency and parallels while also being pretty cheap at this point, so it is highly recommended to get. You will most likely only need to build one of this.
Lastly, there are some multiblocks not mentioned previously that are possible to craft now that you have a cleanroom up and running:
- Oil Cracking Unit : Replaces the hydrogen and steam cracking recipes that were done in the Chemical Reactor in previous tiers. It provides power cost reduction and bonus outputs. This is absolutely worth it for anyone using Oil to produce chemicals such as Ethylene.
- Large Sifter : The first unlockable ore processor. It provides a massive boost to speed in the form of raw time reduction as well as parallels. In addition, sifting is a mandatory step in recycling and processing with the platline which is unlocked in the next tier.
- Dissection Apparatus : Large scale Extractor. This machine is likely to be more niche for the average player, but the slow speed of the Extractor singleblock easily makes this a worthwhile investment for lines such as Glowflower processing.
- TurboCan Pro : Replaces the Fluid Canner and Canner singleblock machines. This machine may have very few uses, but it removes a potential bottleneck in canning fuel cells for players investing in IC2 Nuclear Reactors later on.
- Big Barrel Brewery : Replaces the Brewer. The likeliest use for this machine will be mass production of Lubricant, as it is necessary for the operation of Cutting Machines as well as Ore Drilling Plants, or possibly liquor for the industrious big-brained boozer.
Late-HV
Late HV is all about the preparation for obtaining Titanium. By this point, the vacuum freezer is mandatory, as it is necessary for cooling down hot ingots from the EBFs like Nichrome and Titanium.
Preparation for making the rocket
You need a NASA workbench and a Implosion Compressor for your first rocket. You will find that the NASA Workbench is a particularly arduous craft that for some reason requires you to use GT tools in a crafting grid in HV. On the other hand, the Implosion Compressor should be trivial for the average player, regardless of setup.
The amount of explosives needed for use with the Implosion Compressor is non-trivial, though. You will be expending several stacks of TNT. If your energy setup is based on benzene, you will find that obtaining enough toluene for TNT will be trivial if you upgrade your setup to use a Distillation Tower instead of single-block distilleries. However, if your energy setup is based on oil, you will need some additional processing steps-- diverting some Heavy Fuel for use in a distillery or Distillation Tower will likely be the best way.
You'll need 37 T1 heavy-duty alloy plates and a ton of additional materials. Check the quest book. You'll need a T1 rocket, an oxygen equipment set with 2 light oxygen tanks (only 1 is very risky for resource collecting), an oxygen collector and compressor, a fuel loader, and 9 landing pads.
Blast Off \O/
You did it! You crafted your first rocket ever in this modpack. Now you need to fuel it with 5 cells worth of cetane-boosted diesel. Note that rocket will produce a huge amount of pollution if launched. When you land, you should find yourself in a lander. YOU MUST HOLD THE SPACE BAR (or you will die and lose your rocket) to slow down the lander. You should keep your descent velocity to less than 20 m/s to avoid exploding yourself on landing. Try to find the Ilmenite vein (good source of Titanium and Chrome), Bauxite (for Ilmenite and a lot of Aluminium), and Neodymium (for EV+ motors, Fluorine, Phosphorus, and Rare Earth elements that you need later in the game).
End Of HV
After collection of ores from the Moon, check NEI on how to make Titanium (you process everything into Rutile then react it with Carbon Dust and Chlorine). You will need a stack for turning in the titanium quest to enter the EV tier in the questbook. Note that you must cool Titanium using a Vacuum Freezer after smelting in the EBF.
Spending some time now looking for a Moon dungeon is an excellent idea too. The mobs are not tough if you've been keeping up at all with your armor, weapons, and health bar. In addition, you are guaranteed to find a T2 rocket schematic in the loot chest (which you absolutely need to progress out of early EV in a standard run), and the quest book will grant you access to your own personal dimension!
Infrastructure for processing Rutile into Titanium, and Bauxite specifically is recommended, as they are relatively simple multi-step processes and their reactants (not all of Bauxite's, though) can be recycled very simply. Remember, you will be consuming dozens of stacks of Titanium in EV!
Side Objectives
While there are many upgrades to single block machines and entirely new multi-blocks to craft, not all of them are absolutely necessary to craft in order to progress to EV. However, some of these do provide excellent quality of life changes.
Open Computers Crop Breeding
See the main page here . After finishing the cleanroom, you will have all of the infrastructure necessary to build the crop breeding robot, although you will need epoxid as well as some progression in Thaumcraft. Note that this is an expensive build, especially if you have zero prior progression in Open Computers! The complexity and cost of materials rivals that of the NASA Workbench. However, following the quest book as you gather the components will slightly reduce costs.
When completed, the crop breeder robot is capable of breeding a variety of new crops, statting them up, and even duplicating them for you! The only inputs required after the initial setup are a large number of crop sticks and fuel for the generator.
Chlorine Automation
You will quickly find that HV is completely miserable to progress through without a steady source of chlorine. Luckily, there are good sources of chlorine everywhere. You have several different options, ranging from large amounts of non-renewable resources such as salt ores and Sodalite, or renewable sources such as the IC2 crops Tearstalks and Saltyroot. In all cases, the setup is incredibly cheap: process it into Salt / Rock Salt / Salt Water (Rock Salt is the most efficient by far), then electrolyze it! Although you will be using a large amount of Chlorine in this tier, you will probably never use more than a Super Tank I's worth of it to progress to EV.
Bee Upgrades
The Industrial Apiary is now possible to craft, which is much faster than the base apiary.
Blood Magic
If you are doing a no-rocket run, this mod is one of the only avenues to progress into EV, as summoning meteors is how you will obtain resources such as Titanium. Doing so may increase your warp effects.
Thaumcraft
Additional wand upgrades become possible, as you can now craft the required screws. If you have not progressed at all in Thaumcraft, consider it! There are huge quality of life changes that are only accessible through Thaumcraft progression, such as wings or Boots of the Traveler.
The End and pre-Moon Titanium
Diagram showing processing steps for making Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. EBF - Electric Blast Furnace; LCR - Large Chemical Reactor; DT - Distillation Tower.
Eyes of Ender can be made in an HV Chemical Reactor and used to find and activate the End Portal. After defeating the Ender Dragon, the player can travel to the Far End Asteroids where they will occasionally find veins of Naquadah Ore. This allows the player to produce Titanium Ingots without traveling to the Moon.
Raw Naquadah Ore goes through the usual ore processing and becomes Naquadah Oxide Mixture Dust. Two dust can be processed in the Electric Blast Furnace with 3000L of Fluoroantimonic Acid to produce 4 Titanium Trifluoride Dust, which is then put back into the EBF, which must be overclocked to EV , with 3000L of Hydrogen to get a Hot Titanium Ingot. Cool the ingot in a Vacuum Freezer to obtain a Titanium Ingot.
The production of Fluoroantimonic Acid is an involved process which requires a Large Chemical Reactor that is overclocked to EV. A Distillation Tower is not necessary for the production of Antimony Pentachloride but will refund all of the Ether used in the production of Antimony Trichloride Solution.
The diagram to the right shows the processing steps for obtaining Titanium Ingots from Naquadah Ore. Note that Ethylene and Hydrogen Sulfide are considered inputs, rather than being part of the production chain, as they can be obtained in great quantities from processing Oil and its byproducts.

documents.text:
Extreme Voltage (EV) is the fourth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, several mechanics are introduced such as Applied Energistics 2 (abbreviated as AE2) and the IndustrialCraft 2 Nuclear Reactors . This tier is largely centered around three big goals: starting an AE2 setup, traveling to Mars for new and important resources, and developing centralized electric infrastructure. It introduces several new multiblocks which greatly speed up many processes, but especially ore processing with the introduction of the Industrial Centrifuge , Industrial Maceration Stack , Ore Washing Plant , and others.
Introduction
In the previous tier HV , the main goal was to be able to source titanium. This was done through conventional means such as building a T1 rocket and flying to the moon to collect ores, or other more esoteric means such as bees.
Having the ability to source and smelt titanium unlocks a wide range of new technologies. AE2 is introduced as a way to massively simplify your storage management and begin autocrafting. Note that most of the AE2 machines require titanium, so be prepared to mass produce titanium if you want to use AE2. The mechanics introduced by AE2 are incredibly important to the remainder of the game, so it's recommended to do some reading on best practices. See this subsection of the Automation article for additional information.
With the introduction of the Nuclear Reactor, it is possible to create reactors with designs that generate massive amounts of power on-tier. See the Nuclear Reactor's sample chart for more information. Other than the nuclear reactor, six new large engines become available as alternative means of power.
Lastly, an important note to keep in mind when entering this tier is that this is where many players get burnt out because of how difficult it is to get through this tier. Unlike the transition between the HV and MV tiers, EV is a big jump from HV to EV in terms of energy and resources needed. So be sure to build and prepare your automated systems (and mass-produce resources) if you haven't done so already, because manual crafting has likely become a very taxing task in this tier. You will want to overproduce resources and essential components such as titanium, steel, motors, etc., to make it easier and save time for you to make something you need rather than go back to mining after finding out you don't have enough resources repeatedly. Lastly, if you don't want to get burnt out and want to continue playing, do not rush into EV and the rest of the future tiers. Take your time.
Progression
Titanium Production
Continued from the start of EV with a stack of titanium, you might want to increase your titanium production by chemical bathing ilmenite with sulfuric acid using an EV chemical bath, the resulting byproduct can be electrolysed to get the sulfuric acid back, forming a closed loop where the only input is crushed ilmenite ore. After getting a somewhat stable supply of titanium, you can actually start the EV tier.
You might've started epoxy and basic platline (platinum only); if not, start building as this is a good time to build it.
Tip: if you are using LCR for the platline, you can replace the need for centrifuge with it, which saves the cost of making an industrial centrifuge.
Energy crisis - part 1
You might've found you are struggling to power up those EV single block machines with just several HV generators (either automated or not). If your main energy production is from oil, it's recommended to build a multiblock combustion engine and upgrade to cetane-boosted diesel if you didn't in HV. It costs about 4 stacks of titanium to make and without boosting with oxygen, produces 2048EU/t at 100% efficiency, and if boosted with oxygen, produces 6144EU/t at 150% efficiency. Because of the boosting mechanism, it's recommended to keep it boosting. It also requires a small amount of lubricant to run.
Another option is large gas turbine. It runs at efficiency based on the turbine you put into the controller. The gas input must be close to the optimal flow rate the turbine describes, or efficiency will drop. There is also a replacement, the oxidation fuel unit, where it's the same but does not need a turbine but needs oxygen to run but produces steam, but it's not recommended because it only produces 2048EU/t while costing more than the gas turbine. Also, its efficiency caps at 100% while large gas turbines are based on the turbine and can easily go beyond 100% efficiency.
If you want to make platline or got some platinum, you can build your first nuclear generator. You can check the Nuclear Reactor page to find what design that fits best for you. I recommend you to use the 1280EU/t design as it only needs 4 chambers (3 chambers for the main block). Build as many as you need as the reactor is pretty cheap in both maintaining and its build cost.
Radon Loop
Radon is a new resource introduced in EV. There are 2 main ways to source radon in this tier. The first way is radium decay, which is extremely slow and requires sifting specific ores. The second is the radon loop, which needs Pu-239 which is somewhat time consuming to get in itself, and has a much higher setup cost, but is more permanent as your future radon is produced this way.
The radon loop is found as an LCR recipe that takes a Pu-239 ingot, Uranium 238 dust, and air and converts it into Pu-239 dust and radon. The Pu-239 dust can be smelted in any machine that does furnace recipes to recycle the Plutonium.
Mid EV
After finishing building those lines and you have increased your energy production, you can start to make nano circuits. You have to first upgrade your HV circuit assembler into an EV counterpart, and make nano CPU wafer. It's recommended to make it in LCR with a stable power supply because it needs 60 seconds to make one without overclocking. You will have to make 8 nano mainframes for the 2 EV field generators required for the tier 2 rocket computer.
You might've also noticed that EV field generator requires HSS-G. For getting tungsten, first collect a large amount of endstone, crush it and centrifuge the dust to get some tungstate dust, then make an EV autoclave for the first step of the tungsten line, separating lithium out of tungstate dust. Then, pass the liquid into chemical reactor with calcium chloride to make wolframite dust, then pass in hydrochloric acid to form tungsten hydroxide then process it twice in the EBF to get tungsten dust, or ingot if you want to pulverize it down into dust.
Then, blend tungsten dust with steel dust to get tungstensteel dust, and blend again with some miscellaneous dusts to get HSS-G dust. You have to make TPV coil upgrade for your EBF before processing HSS-G dust in it. Then cool it off using vacuum freezer to get the ingot. HSS-G is also used for the next tier of coils, but these are gated behind the IV assembler.
Side quest: AE
You can also start applied energistics with the supply of titanium. You have to make a controller, a drive, and a bunch of cables for your first network to get working, also ME crafting interface.
You might follow this instead: Applied Energistics 2
Side quest 2: Multiblock ore processing
As you entered EV, you gained access to multiblock counterparts of centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer/chemical bath, and crusher. They are way more efficient compared to their singleblock variants, however they require large amounts of resources like Titanium and most are gated behind TPV coils, so they're listed here instead of in early EV. If your main resource income is from bees, centrifuge is recommended over all other multiblocks as it speeds up centrifuging combs significantly.
Your second rocket / Late-EV
After getting the EV field generator you needed for the rocket computer, it's time to build your second rocket. It's a pretty straightforward step. If you forgot or didn't get much meteoric iron, you have to get back to the moon and mine some. I recommend you to have 12 stacks or 45 stacks if you don't want to go back to the moon again for meteoric iron (also for t3 rocket). With the exception of several new parts, which are booster and t2 landing module, the rest goes the same as t1 rocket but is more expensive.
You only need a trip to mars for you to get all the resources needed. Also, T2 lander doesn't need you to slow down when approaching as it's a balloon that bounces after it reaches the surface. Your mission there is to collect desh vein (it also has tungsten ore), tungsten vein (also provides lithium), and pitchblende vein (also provides thorium) if you didn't get enough uranium by centrifuging thorium ore. Remember to explore mars more for finding the mars dungeon which contains the T3 rocket blueprint.
Energy crisis - part 2
After making power generation for EV, you found out that you are constantly wasting fuel because nuclear reactor / multiblock generators are constantly burning fuel. You will have to make a control system with a huge battery to efficiently use the generator.
You will be making a Lapotronic Supercapacitor for energy storage. Other types of energy storage, like single block storage, are not recommended due to their cost to store huge amounts of power. It will passively drain a trivial amount of energy (~30EU/t if 1x3x3 IV capacitor). You only need normal borosilicate glass to use IV and EV capacitor.
End of EV
After a trip back to mars full of ores (and also loots), you should have enough tungsten to get ready for IV. Also, you can make EV superconductor. It's cheap enough in late-EV, with superior performance compared to other wires. You also have to get graphene. It needs tons of silicon due to the amount of wafer it requires to craft (32 for P-doped wafer, 8 for Nq-doped).
Good luck with your journey to IV!
Side Quests
-Eliminate microcrafting and improve automation and QoL with AE2 .
-Build advanced processing lines for Ilmenite and Bauxite.
-Make a Multiblock Miner for higher ore output.
-Make various GT++ Multiblock versions of singleblocks such as the Bending Machine, Centrifuge, Lathe and Maceration Stack.

documents.text:
Insane Voltage (IV) is the fifth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. In this tier, multiple new multiblocks and mechanics are introduced, such as the Assembly Line , the Precise Assembler , and many more. This is also the tier where many parts of magic (Thaumcraft, etc.) are unlocked for players to use; however, as always, watch your warp effects if you have been getting warp. While transitioning from the old tier to a new tier is usually the hard part, the IV tier is by far the hardest tier to get through. If you managed to get through EV tier, prepare yourself because this tier requires a very heavy transition in almost every aspect of your base, including infrastructure and crafting. At this point, manual crafting is no longer a feasible option. With this being said, be prepared for a big change to your base!
Prerequisites before continuing
IV is a very tough tier which requires large amounts of infrastructure in order to progress smoothly. Some things you will want to have done in EV are:
- A large AE2 system that can handle storage, automation, and autocrafting. (Some of the things in this list can be automated with AE2 by simply patterning them)
- Automated the first part of the platline in order to have a large supply of Platinum available.
- Automated Tungsten processing, as well as large amounts of raw/processed tungsten ores (Tungstate and Scheelite).
- Automated plastics, including Polyethylene, PTFE, and Epoxid.
- Automated Graphene for IV motors.
- A robust automated power generation and distribution system that can support early IV infrastructure, and is easily expanded later in the tier.
- Automated ore processing in order to easily obtain bulk basic resources.
If you find yourself not meeting some of these requirements, try going back and filling them out before coming back to IV progression. Some of the things on this list may be helpful for getting other things on this list (e.g getting Platinum is integral to AE2, and automated plastics means that you can do much more processing with virtually infinite LCRs and circuits)
Power
Storage and Distribution
Although it is possible to create centralized power storage and distribution infrastructure in earlier tiers, IV is the tier where any player who hasn't done so already should create said centralized power infrastructure. Although other approaches exist, the most common way to do so is to use a Lapotronic Supercapacitor (LSC) as the main battery, fed directly from power generation (to minimize cable loss), and then distribute power outwards from the LSC to the rest of the base using a "power spine". This power spine consists of a cable, or multiple cables if additional capacity is needed, with a high maximum amperage and a voltage usually greater than the player's current voltage tier. Power is transformed up when leaving the LSC to minimize cable loss and take full advantage of the cable's capacity, and transformed down for usage close to the actual machines. In IV, typical power spine cables are 16x versions of most LuV cables, such as Vanadium-Gallium, HSS-G, or Niobium-Titanium, depending on which is the easiest for the player to produce in bulk.
Generation
In order to take full advantage of this power storage and distribution infrastructure, it is necessary for the player to also greatly expand their power generation, usually to hundreds of thousands of EU/t by the end of the tier. In order to accomplish this, IV unlocks a wealth of new power generation multiblocks, as well as processing multiblocks that greatly simplify the process of generating fuel, while also saving on power compared to their singleblock counterparts. Players using Benzene should upgrade to Nitrobenzene if they have not already, upgrade to better turbine materials such as HSS-S or HSS-E, and use new multiblocks like the Industrial Electrolyzer and Dangote Distillus . Players using oil can benefit from the Extreme Combustion Engine by upgrading to High-Octane Gasoline as their fuel, and can use the Dangote Distillus to improve the speed and efficiency of making that fuel. Nuclear Reactors remain a viable means of generating power as well, and players using steam gain access to the XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine to generate power from Superheated Steam more compactly. In addition, many unconventional means of power generation unlock in IV, such as the Deep Earth Heating Pump , Rocketdyne F-1A Engine , and Solar Tower .
Infrastructure
IV is the first major "infrastructure tier", a term used for tiers that require the player to make especially large investments in expanding their infrastructure in order to complete the tier and be prepared for future tiers. As a result, the biggest focus of IV is in the many ways to improve said infrastructure that are unlocked in the tier.
New Multiblocks
IV unlocks most of the processing multiblocks not already available in EV , which can be used to greatly improve processing speed, simplify autocrafting with non-consumed items, bolster processing lines, and perform tier skips. As soon as the player is able to make IV singleblock machines, multiblock forms of the following machines open up:
- Zyngen (Alloy Smelter)
- Industrial Electrolyzer (Electrolyzer)
- Magnetic Flux Exhibitor (Electromagnetic Separator and Polarizer, requires iridium)
- Industrial Extrusion Machine (Extruder)
- Density^2 (Implosion Compressor, requires ZPM circuits)
- Industrial Mixing Machine (Mixer)
- Industrial Wire Factory (Wiremill)
The remaining multiblocks largely require the Alloy Blast Smelter (ABS), a new machine that can create various alloys in fluid form that are otherwise unobtainable. Notably, it cannot run higher-tier recipes by using multiple Energy Hatches like the EBF can, which means the player will need to either complete the platline or manually process iridium in order to run IV-tier recipes. The multiblocks made available by using the ABS are:
- Industrial Cutting Factory (Cutting Machine and Slicing Machine)
- Dangote Distillus (Distillery and Distillation Tower)
- Industrial Sledgehammer (Forge Hammer)
- Fluid Shaper (Fluid Solidifier and Tool Casting Machine)
- Amazon Warehousing Depot (Packager and Unpackager)
- Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver (Precision Laser Engraver)
- Volcanus (improved version of the Electric Blast Furnace)
- Cryogenic Freezer (improved version of the Vacuum Freezer)
The Precise Assembler , a multiblock version of the Assembling Machine, is also unlocked in IV, although it requires the full platline as well as access to naquadah. Despite these costs, it is extremely worthwhile, due to its double speed, 16 parallels in IV, and ability to greatly simplify the need to manage programmed circuits for recipes.
On top of these processing machines, there are also new machines that can be used to gather resources for the ever-increasing demands of the tier:
- Boldarnator (multiblock Rock Breaker)
- Extreme Industrial Greenhouse (crops)
- Tree Growth Simulator (wood and other tree products)
- Zhuhai Fishing Port (fish and fishing byproducts)
- Tier 2 of the Ore Drilling Plant
- Tier 4 of the Fluid Drilling Rig
The final multiblock in IV is the Assembly Line , which requires robust infrastructure in order to produce the 90 ZPM circuits needed for even the minimum viable length in a reasonable amount of time. It serves as the gate to the LuV tier, as well as a way to test if the player's infrastructure has been sufficiently developed.
Circuits
IV contains many improvements to circuit production, but this is paired with a circuit demand far exceeding any prior tiers. The new circuit line, Quantumprocessors, is available as soon as an IV Circuit Assembler is crafted, but they require large quantities of platinum and radon to be made in bulk. The Quantumprocessor Mainframe is also the first ZPM circuit available, and it is needed for machines like the Volcanus as well as the Assembly Line that gates LuV.
In addition to the new circuit line, lower tier circuits also get upgrades. Multiblocks like the Industrial Wire Factory , Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver , and Precise Assembler greatly speed the process of making circuit components. Naquadah, which can be found either rarely in End asteroids or on the Asteroids dimension with a tier 3 rocket, can be processed slowly in the EBF to yield Naquadah Nuggets, which can be used to make the next tier of silicon boule and thereby unlock better wafer recipes. One of these recipes is SoC Wafers, which are used in better LV and MV circuit recipes. Advanced SMDs, although requiring advanced materials such as PBI and platline metals, can also be used to replace regular SMDs in earlier circuit recipes, allowing them to be crafted twice as fast and with a quarter of the SMD requirements.
Because of the very high circuit demands of late IV and LuV, it is highly recommended to parallelize circuit crafting by using multiple Circuit Assemblers, as the multiblock Circuit Assembly Line is unavailable until LuV.
Smelting
IV is a tier that demands a lot of capacity to smelt ingots in the Electric Blast Furnace and cool them in the Vacuum Freezer , but it is also a tier that unlocks major upgrades to meet this demand. HSS-G Coils are available as soon as the Assembling Machine is crafted, and should be a priority upgrade for the energy discounts, new recipes, and perfect overclocks they can reach. HSS-S Coils are not required, but are unlocked upon completing the platline, and are very valuable for the same reasons. IV is also a good time to look at upgrading beyond helium for those EBF recipes that require a noble gas; these gases can be made with liquid Overworld/Nether Air processing, bees, or the Radon loop. The more interesting upgrades, however, revolve around using better versions of the EBF and VF that allow greater throughput.
Volcanus
One of these upgrades is the Volcanus , a superior version of the EBF which is over twice as fast, supports up to 8 parallels, and has a 10% energy discount. However, it requires 10 L/s of Blazing Pyrotheum to run, which means that fluid needs to be automated before upgrading to Volcani; the main ways to do this are either to use the Pyrotheum Bee, or automatically mix coal dust, sulfur, blaze powder, and redstone into Pyrotheum Dust and fluid extract it. It's also worth noting that, unlike the regular EBF, the Volcanus does not receive a heat bonus from voltage, which means a few recipes can require a regular EBF to run.
Mega Vacuum Freezer
The Mega Vacuum Freezer (MVF) is an upgrade to the regular Vacuum Freezer which has greatly improved throughput: like most Mega multiblocks, it can run up to 256 recipes in parallel, and allows for multi-amp and laser hatches to get the power to run those recipes, as well as allowing tierskipping multiple tiers with sufficient amperage. Although mega multiblocks are generally not recommended to build until laser infrastructure is unlocked, the MVF is the exception to this. This is because Vacuum Freezer recipes generally require lower voltage tiers than their respective EBF recipes, meaning that it is possible to utilize all 256 parallels as early as IV with a multi-amp energy hatch.
Mega Electric Blast Furnace and Cryogenic Freezer
These two multiblocks are the counterparts of the Mega Vacuum Freezer and Volcanus, respectively, and can be used in IV to upgrade smelting, but are generally considered inferior to the options above. The Mega Electric Blast Furnace (MEBF or MBF) can run 256 parallels and use multi-amp and laser energy hatches, like the MVF, but unlike the MVF (which only requires aluminium) it requires a huge number of coil and tiered glass blocks to form, making it far more expensive. However, it does have the ability to tier skip multiple tiers, and receives heat bonuses for every tier, which can be valuable for smelting otherwise unavailable materials. The Cryogenic Freezer is a Vacuum Freezer with double the speed and 4 parallels, but it requires 10 L/s Gelid Cryotheum to run, which is an extra logistical challenge not present for the Mega Vacuum Freezer, and it lacks support for multi-amp energy hatches.
Progression Goals
The Platline
The Platinum Line , known as the Platline for short, is the central chemical line of IV, and is one of the most complex chemical lines in the entire pack, with approximately 50 steps in total. Although the first part of the platline, which yields Platinum itself, should be done already in EV, the rest, for Palladium, Rhodium, Ruthenium, Iridium, and Osmium, is required to progress into further tiers as well as for many useful upgrades and quality of life improvements within IV. These include the IV Energy Hatch, the Infinite Spray Can (a spray can with access to all 16 colors and infinite uses, for coloring cables), the Vajra (a tool to instantly break any block), and the HSS-S Coils for upgrading the Electric Blast Furnace and other multiblocks. It is possible to run the platline manually as well, in order to obtain small amounts of platline materials to afford key upgrades without needing to build the entire line immediately; for example, an IV Energy Hatch or two to be able to run certain otherwise impossible recipes, such as Nitinol 60 in an ABS to be able to make a HILE .
Other chemical lines
Polybenzimidazole
Although the platline is the foremost line in IV, it is not the only one. The other major lines introduced in IV are the plastic Polybenzimidazole (usually abbreviated to PBI) and various rare earth processing lines used to obtain otherwise rare materials. Although PBI is not strictly required in IV, it is needed for the Tier 2 Thermal Padding that almost every planet from Tier 3 and above demands, and can be used to greatly improve circuit production by making Advanced SMDs, and parallelize multiblocks with the Linked Input Bus.
Rare Earths
The rare earth lines are never required, beyond basic samarium processing (which is very short and easy to make, but has poor yield and no byproducts), but are useful for many otherwise rare materials. The simplest of these lines is advanced samarium processing, which greatly improves the yield from Samarium Ore Concentrate Dust and yields byproducts of Cerium, Neodymium, and Lanthanum, and can be upgraded in LuV to further double the Samarium yield. The other two rare earth lines are the Monazite Line (monaline) and the Bastnasite Line (bastline), which can convert the respective crushed ores into a variety of rare earths and other materials: Zirconium, Cerium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Holmium, Terbium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Bastline, and Hafnia, Zirconium, Cerium, Europium, Gadolinium, and Samarium for the Monaline. Of these materials, only Samarium is required to enter LuV, but the others have a variety of uses in LuV and beyond. Note that all of these lines require automating the Dissolution Tank .
Rockets
Unlike most tiers, IV contains two different tiers of rockets and associated sets of planets that they unlock. The Tier 3 Rocket is available early in the tier, only being gated behind the IV Assembling Machine to make some of the parts. The Tier 4 Rocket, on the other hand, requires the Assembly Line, meaning it is unavailable until just before the start of LuV. In addition, both tiers require an upgraded rocket fuel, Dense Hydrazine, in order to use, which will require building a Chemical Plant for players who opted to use Cetane-Boosted Diesel for the first two tiers. Most planets from Tier 3 onwards also require an upgraded set of Thermal Padding, which needs PBI to make, and the Tier 4 planet Venus requires a full set of armor with the SpaceSuit property. For a full list of resources available on the Tier 3 and 4 planets, see the Planets page. The Tier 3 rocket also unlocks the ability to make a space station over Jupiter, although the Tier 4 rocket is required to make the Planetary Gas Siphon that makes such a space station useful.
Magic Mods
IV is also the point at which much of the lategame content in many magic mods becomes available to players willing to invest into them.
In Thaumcraft , most of the Kami equipment that requires Ichor becomes available with Osmiridium, an alloy that is made from Osmium and Iridium and smelted in an LuV-tier EBF. This includes the best available wand materials, a set of powerful tools and armor, and the Pure Tear and Purification Talisman, both of which can be used to solve warp (the former once and the latter continuously). The Pure Tear can also be obtained through the Quest Book using one Osmiridium Ingot, which can help players struggling with warp who aren't close to obtaining Ichor and being able to craft it themselves.
In Blood Magic , the tier 5 and 6 Blood Orbs can be crafted once platline materials are obtained, which unlocks the ability to summon many more meteors and to reach almost all of the mod's content, including advanced rituals and spell parts. Furthermore, some of the most useful meteors require IV machines or components to summon, such as the IV Scanner meteor, which contains huge amounts of platline dusts.
In Botania , IV is the first tier where it's possible to summon the Gaia Guardian, although the naquadah that is required can make it challenging to afford until a later tier.
Word of Caution
An important note to keep in mind when reaching this tier: This is another tier where most players get burnt out. If you managed not to get burnt out in the EV tier, you may have more chances to get burnt out in this tier. Compared to EV, this tier is much longer and resource-intensive, so do not rush into the IV tier if you want to avoid getting burned out. Take your time.

documents.text:
Ludicrous Voltage (LuV) is the sixth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier is largely centered around building the infrastructure necessary to construct the first tier of Fusion Reactor , as well as the new items and machines gated by fusion. This is the first tier where the Assembly Line is used to craft on-tier components as well as highly advanced machines. In addition, the costs and crafting trees for machines are even larger than in previous tiers, making fully automated on-demand crafting with AE2 absolutely necessary. The massive demand for robust infrastructure continues for the rest of the game; arrays of Volcanus consuming on-tier voltage are highly suggested.
Progression
LuV is a much smaller tier compared to IV in terms of different milestones. The capstone of this tier is the Mk I. Fusion Reactor; it enables crafting Europium, which in turn gates T5 rockets, europium-doped wafers, the Crystal circuit line, and more.
LuV Components
Unlike all previous tiers, LuV components must be crafted in a multiblock dedicated to complex crafts: the Assembly Line . The Assembly Line requires data sticks corresponding to crafts in order to craft anything. The data sticks for LuV components are created by scanning their IV counterparts inside a Scanner singleblock .
Naquadah Processing
The LuV energy hatch recipe requires 4 ingots worth of molten Naquadah. Naquadah is obtained from Naquadah Oxide Mixture-- a dust obtained from Naquadah Ore veins on T4 planets. Prior to LuV, the only way to obtain Naquadah was through an IV EBF recipe which produces one nugget from two NOM dust and is miserably slow.
In LuV, a naquadah processing line becomes possible to set up, which greatly increases the efficiency of NOM to Naquadah conversion. Most of the central steps do not require LuV voltage, but one of the central machines is strictly gated to LuV: the Neutron Activator .
A minimum height Neutron Activator.
There are also two related materials that are also obtained from Naquadah Ore: Enriched Naquadah and Naquadria. These materials have similar processing steps, but are processed separately from different dusts. Their lines are possible to construct although optional in LuV. They may be attractive due to the byproducts of indium, barium, and trinium. However, they must be built to progress in ZPM.
Neutron Activator
The Neutron Activator is a multiblock that is central to the processing of naquadah, enriched naquadah, and naquadria. It requires the Precise Assembler to craft. On top of this, the Precise Assembler needs to have Mk I. casings in order to be able to craft the Neutron Activator and its required components. The Neutron Activator has a unique mechanic not seen in previous multiblocks-- the height of the Neutron Activator is used to determine the speed of recipes, not the input voltage.
Fusion Reactor
A Fusion Reactor.
The capstone of LuV is the construction of a Fusion Reactor. Once Europium is obtained, it becomes possible to craft ZPM components. The Fusion Reactor is expensive--a single Mk I. requires over 4,000 LuV superconductors. Despite this expense, additional fusion reactors become attractive immediately, both for other materials and potentially to generate power.
Fusion Reactors have a unique mechanic in that they require a large amount of EU to begin processing a single type of recipe, typically in the hundreds of millions of EU. This is largely intended to penalize recipe switching or letting a recipe stop running, meaning that passive production of materials via fusion is the most attractive way to use Fusion Reactors. Fusion Reactors also have a very limited rate of power intake; it can take several minutes before a new recipe can run. As a result, resources that are crafted on demand should use a large batch size.
The available recipes in the Mk1 fusion reactor, in rough order of importance, are as follows:
- Europium is the most important recipe by far, since it's needed in large quantities for all ZPM components. It should be passively produced in a dedicated reactor due to its slow rate of production, taking nearly 6 minutes to produce for a single ZPM motor.
- Helium Plasma is not strictly necessary in LuV, but will be required in ZPM to smelt Neutronium and in UV for the Waterline . In LuV, it can also be used for power in a singleblock plasma generator or Large Plasma Turbine , or in further fusion recipes for Sunnarium and Boron Plasma.
- Duranium is not necessary yet either, but is an extremely powerful material for steam and gas turbine rotors. It is needed for Quantum Anomalies in the Cyclotron, and is used in ZPM to make Tritanium, which is needed for Void Miners and the Tier 6 Rocket.
- Calcium Plasma, Boron Plasma, Neon Plasma, and Force Plasma are part of the "plasma chain" of fusion recipes, which extends through the first three tiers of fusion reactors, and produces plasmas with much better stats than simple Helium Plasma for power generation.
- Sunnarium can be produced using Helium Plasma, providing an alternative to methods like bees , breeder reactors , or the Molecular Transformer .
- Osmium can be fused from Tungsten, although it is extremely slow at nearly 2 minutes per ingot, and therefore needs to be passive to be usable at all.
- There are fusion recipes for Iron, Chrome, and Platinum, but those materials are cheap enough that they're never worth using.
For information on additional plasma options to generate power and to make additional materials, see this spreadsheet .
Power
Storage and Distribution
The next tier of Lapotronic Supercapacitor capacitor is unlocked; it provides a massive boost to the total energy storage capacity. Vanadium-gallium cables are still recommended in this tier as a backbone due to their relatively low loss and amperage.
Generation
Like the previous tier IV , power generation capacity should follow the trend of exponential increase in order to accommodate the increasing number of energy-intensive processes. Several new multiblocks are now possible to construct which keeps some older power generation methods viable:
- XL Turbo Gas Turbine
- Universal Chemical Fuel Engine
- Whakawhiti Wera XL
- XL Turbo HP Steam Turbine
Despite the upgrade to the UCFE, power generation from oil processing begins to fall off after this tier. Nitrobenzene gains a massive buff from the XLGT largely due to scalability, since turbines no longer need to be manually replaced, and only one multi-amp / laser dynamo is needed for a multiblock that generates 16x the power of a single LGT. Like oil, this is the last tier where benzene gains a direct upgrade. Lastly, Vacuum Reactors gain a massive buff in "The Core". "The Core" is the final fuel rod upgrade for vacuum reactors; it is extremely dangerous due to its heat generation, but produces a massive amount of energy.
In addition, a new method of power generation becomes available: plasma. Plasma produced by a fusion reactor can generate power in two different ways: placed into an Extreme Heat Exchanger in order to produce supercritical steam, or placed into a Large Plasma Turbine which directly generates power. Both methods will transform the plasma into its liquid / gas state, which can be potentially useful. Building a compact fusion reactor for power generation is the strongest source of energy available in LuV, albeit by far the most expensive.
Infrastructure
Resource Shortages
Aside from the new materials, all of the Platline materials will be needed in massive amounts. Ruridit as well as rhodium-plated palladium are used in huge quantities for even the most basic components and machines. Yttrium, Samarium, Neodymium, and many other rare earths will be needed in large amounts as well. However, mining many of the rare earths directly is not yet possible, so alternative production methods must be explored, such as Rare Earth dehydration, bees, and blood magic meteors. Radon will also be needed in large amounts, so the radon loop should be built if one has not done so.
Waterline
The Water Purification Plant, hub of the Waterline.
LuV introduces the Waterline , a collection of multiblocks which produce increasingly pure water. The first two tiers of water, Filtered and Ozonated, speed up the cutting and engraving of wafers. The first grade of water is necessary for LuV progression as it is needed for the Netherite line. The second grade is optional at LuV, but it improves the yield and speed of the Nefarious Oil step, so it is recommended to invest in it. They will also be needed later on as the Waterline is even more relevant at higher tiers where high tier water is necessary for the production of chips.
Circuits
After the completion of the fusion reactor, it becomes possible to manufacture Crystal circuits. These circuits have a unique automation challenge due to how their "CPU" component is crafted; it requires a loop of autoclaving and forge hammering. In addition, the standard method of creating the CPUs requires molten europium. The Crystalprocessor Mainframe is the first UV circuit available.
Other Multiblocks
- Circuit Assembly Line : Creates a large amount of circuits faster and often with a reduced cost than a regular circuit assembler. Pre-fusion, a Circuit Assembly Line only provides a speed improvement and so is optional. Post-fusion they are necessary to create the new circuit line, Crystalprocessors, and all circuit lines after.
- Cyclotron : This multiblock is shaped similar to a fusion reactor, and generates particles. A notable use for the cyclotron is to generate quantum anomalies to make Advanced Nitinol. Advanced Nitinol is needed for the Matter Fabrication CPU as well as other ZPM and higher multiblocks. Note that in 2.9, this multiblock has been depreciated and replaced by the Large Hadron Collider .
- Industrial Autoclave : A multi-block autoclave, it is a massive upgrade to the single-block autoclave with reduced power consumption, as well as increased speed and parallels. It is highly recommended to create the large amount of crystal chips needed for crystal processors, as well as for processing Naquadah at far faster rates.
- Industrial Arc Furnace : A multi-block arc furnace. Although unlocked in LuV, it has few uses, and requires a unique automation challenge with managing electrodes, making its usefulness at this stage questionable, outside of making netherite materials faster.
