documents.text:
Insanely Ultimate Voltage (UIV) is the eleventh electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. Its focus is scaling the DTPF , unlocked in the previous tier, with improved coils and new sources of catalyst, in order to afford more advanced materials and progress to UMV . It also introduces new, extremely powerful multiblocks such as the Forge of the Gods , as well as the final Creative items and the end of Draconic Evolution progression. UIV is generally considered to mark the transition from lategame to endgame.
Progression
DTPF Coils
At the start of UIV, the player's DTPF is likely equipped with a set of Infinity coils, which can be used for the Hypogen loop in addition to being required for Tesseracts. The first goal is to use the Hypogen loop to produce the 19,008 ingots worth of Hypogen required to make Hypogen coils.
With Hypogen coils, new recipes become available, the most notable of which is SpaceTime, needed for the final coil upgrade, Eternal coils. The SpaceTime recipe available with Hypogen coils is incredibly inefficient, requiring one Tesseract, 16 Infinity, 8 Hypogen, and 10 kL of Dimensionally Transcendent Residue for a single ingot of SpaceTime. A much better recipe is unlocked with Eternal coils, which removes the Hypogen input and is four to eight times as efficient on other inputs, including time, but a full Eternal DTPF requires 20,064 ingots of SpaceTime to make, assuming the much better Black Hole Compressor recipe is used for the Eternal Singularities. In order to achieve this, SpaceTime should be passived and overclocked, and spending SpaceTime on anything other than Eternal coils should be avoided whenever possible.
Eternal coils are effectively the gate for UMV because of how much SpaceTime the tier's components use, and because they are needed for UMV Superconductor Base and Shirabon, both materials required in UMV.
Transcendent Plasma Mixer
The Transcendent Plasma Mixer (TPM) is a multiblock specialized for making DTPF catalyst extremely quickly. It can make each tier of catalyst in a single step, taking 5 seconds per recipe, and can run any number of parallels as set in the GUI, similar to the Waterline multiblocks. Rather than drawing power every tick, like most multiblocks, it draws power directly from the wireless network at the start of each recipe cycle; as a result, players who have not already started moving power storage into the wireless network will need to do so to run the TPM. The TPM is very power-hungry, even with its perfectly efficient parallels, and will likely be the largest power consumer in most players' bases in UIV. It is also used to produce three new materials, of which only Creon is relevant in UIV: Creon and its counterpart Mellion are needed for the Godforge.
UMV Circuits
Pico Circuits, the only UMV circuit, can be made in the Assembly Line as soon as it is equipped with UIV Energy Hatches to overclock it to UMV. Each circuit takes 500 seconds, and cannot be run in the Advanced Assembly Line until it has a UMV Laser Target Hatch, so it is recommended to use a large amount of 8-hatched regular Assembly Lines for early Pico Circuits. Another option is to prioritize UMV Laser Hatches with the first few Pico Circuits in order to be able to produce them in an Advanced Assembly Line; Laser Hatches do not require superconductors, and therefore can be made before Eternal Coils, albeit at a steep SpaceTime cost.
Fusion Mk5
The Mk5 Fusion Reactor, optional in UEV, becomes more important in UIV, although still not strictly required. It is primarily needed for the Godforge, which requires Creon (which needs Thorium Plasma), Lead Plasma, and Plutonium 241 Plasma, all of which require a Mk5 Fusion Reactor to make. The Compact Mk5 also provides an at least 4x speedup on all previous fusion recipes, which is especially important for many slow Mk4 recipes that are heavily used in UIV, so it should be prioritized even though it's not strictly required yet.
Black Hole Compressor
The Pseudostable Black Hole Containment Field (typically called the Black Hole Compressor or BHC for short) is a highly advanced multiblock version of the Compressor and Neutronium Compressor. It is required for new, more efficient recipes for the Eternal Singularity, Sphaghettic Singularity, and Cryptic Singularity, as well as for Superdense Plates of some high-tier materials such as SpaceTime and Transcendent Metal. The Eternal Singularity recipe, which only requires 72 L of SpaceTime, is of particular interest due to the requirement for Eternal Singularities for Eternal Coils. However, it is fairly complicated to automate, and requires inserting a Black Hole Seed every time a recipe is run, and a Black Hole Collapser some time after to prevent recipes from being voided; as a result, it is rarely used for recipes that do not require it, despite the large improvements to speed and efficiency that it offers over the Hot Isostatic Pressurization Unit and Neutronium Compressor .
Forge of the Gods
See More: Forge of the Gods
The Forge of the Gods
The Forge of the Gods (Godforge for short) is an extremely powerful multiblock for smelting and related operations. The Godforge itself is only the central structure, and cannot run any recipes; recipes are instead processed by modules that can be fit around the tube-like structure between the front and the rings. Like the TPM, all Godforge modules draw power directly from the wireless network.
The Godforge has an upgrade tree, where upgrades that allow for new modules, improved processing capability, and other improvements can be purchased using a currency called Graviton Shards. Graviton Shards are unlocked by completing milestones relating to using the Godforge and improving its structure. In order to enter UXV, it is necessary to reach the END upgrade, the final upgrade in the Godforge's upgrade tree. Because this requires completing most of the Godforge's milestones, it is recommended to build it and begin progressing its milestones sooner rather than later.
Helioflare Power Forge
The Helioflare Power Forge is a very powerful EBF with access to thousands of parallels and billions of EU/t for each, making slow EBF recipes like Transcendent Metal no longer a bottleneck. It is also required for Saturated Phononic Crystal Solution, which has a heat requirement too high to reach in any other machine, and which is needed for all other Godforge modules.
Helioflux Melting Core
The Helioflux Melting Core is a variant of the Helioflare Power Forge that outputs molten metal directly instead of hot ingots, and therefore allows skipping the often-slow Vacuum Freezer. Other than this output change, the recipes are identical to standard EBF recipes, meaning there is no speed penalty to switching recipes to the Melting Core other than the different stats between each Godforge module. These stats can be seen in the calculator in the main Godforge GUI, but the Melting Core is generally better due to how poorly the Vacuum Freezer scales.
Heliothermal Plasma Fabricator
The Heliothermal Plasma Fabricator converts materials into their plasma forms directly. It can only make simple plasmas at first, and requires Godforge upgrades to unlock T4-T5, multi-step, and exotic plasmas. It can be used to make plasmas that have no fusion recipe, such as Copper Plasma for an improved Metastable Oganesson recipe, as well as to improve on the speed of plasmas whose fusion recipe is particularly slow, such as Calcium Plasma.
Heliofusion Exoticizer
The Heliofusion Exoticizer is used to produce two types of exotic matter: Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) and Magmatter. Both types require a complex automation challenge to be solved in order to produce the material. QGP has only one use before making the Stargate , an improved Rhugnor recipe, making it not a high priority, and Magmatter is only unlocked with the END upgrade but is needed to advance to UXV. Despite the fact that neither material is immediately useful, it is still beneficial to make and place a Heliofusion Exoticizer to advance the Composition milestone.
Infrastructure
Power
UIV continues to scale power demands, causing Naquadah Fuel to begin to fall off and plasma to fall out of viability. However, unlike UEV, it also introduces two new methods of power generation: Dyson Swarms and Antimatter. It also adds the first Wireless Energy Hatches, which greatly simplify power distribution logistics.
Naquadah Fuel
Naqfuel is still viable in UIV, but it struggles to keep up with the new power generation options added in the tier. The DTPF can be used to produce Chromatic Glass and Hypogen for the improved recipes for Naq3 and Naq4, as well as Infinity for Naq5, and with the TPM it is possible to make Creon and Mellion for the improved Naq5 recipe as well. In addition, Transcendent Metal can be used to make Tier 3 coils for the Naquadah Fuel Refinery , which are necessary for the improved Naq5 recipe and quadruple the speed of previous recipes. Naqfuel can also build into Antimatter, as depleted Naq5 and Naq6 are both additives that can be used to improve antimatter production in the SSASS .
Dyson Swarm
The Dyson Swarm Ground Unit
The Dyson Swarm Ground Unit (Dyson) is a new power generation multiblock that is unlocked with UMV circuits. It can produce 337B EU/t when placed on the planet Horus, which is the only place Dysons should be built, at the cost of 3.6 ML of Gelid Cryotheum and 64 Dyson Swarm Modules every hour, as well as one or more Quantum Computers making at least 100,000 Computation. In order to transport the power back from Horus, a Lapotronic Supercapacitor should be used to send it into the wireless network; this can be replaced with an Energized Wireless Dynamo Hatch in UMV.
Antimatter
Antimatter, which is one of the two viable sources of power in the endgame (the other being the Eye of Harmony ), is first unlocked in UIV. Producing power with antimatter requires first generating it using a Semi-Stable Antimatter Stabilization Sequencer with various additives, and then annihilating it with regular matter in a Shielded Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix . Although antimatter can be extremely powerful in later tiers, in UIV it is fairly weak due to not having access to UMV- and UXV-tier additives like Magmatter, Eternity, Shirabon, and UMV Superconductor Base, being limited to only a couple tens of trillions of EU/t, making it much more effort than comparable power production from Dysons.
Wireless Energy
Wireless Energy Hatches can be made using SpaceTime; they are energy hatches that draw power directly from the wireless network, simplifying logistics and preventing lag from wire network calculations. However, in UIV, the only wireless energy hatches available are non-multiamp ones for UEV and below, since UIV Wireless Energy Hatches require UXV circuits, and multi-amp Wireless Energy Hatches require Shirabon. The UIV Capacitor is also unlocked in UIV, and can provide up to 100T EU/t to very power-hungry multiblocks like the DTPF , CoAL , and AAL for which the 1T EU/t of the UEV capacitor can be insufficient.
Crafting Input Proxy
The Crafting Input Proxy is the endgame solution for on-demand parallelization of multiblocks. Crafting Input Proxies can be placed on any multiblock and linked to a Crafting Input Bus or Buffer (Crib) using a Data Stick. When AE2 pushes a recipe to a machine using a Crib, it will push that same recipe to all linked Crafting Input Proxies as well. Crafting Input Proxies do not require power or channels, and an unlimited number of them can be linked to the same Crib, making them extremely powerful for scaling processing capacity to meet the demands of lategame.
Space Elevator
The first Space Elevator improvement available in UIV is Mk3 motors, which only require Transcendent Metal and some UEV components. These motors unlock three new module slots, for a total of 15, requiring the expansion to the Space Elevator to be built in order to use them. They also provide the ability to use upgraded versions of all three module types.
The Mk3 Mining Module works twice as fast as the Mk2 one, but its main selling point is its access to Tier 3-gated asteroids. The most notable resources it unlocks include Americium, Ichorium, Tengam, and pure Platline dusts.
The Mk2 Assembler Module is much faster than its Mk1 counterpart, up to 16 times depending on recipe. It also unlocks improved recipes for Optically Compatible Memory and Optically Perfected CPU that are faster and more efficient, at the cost of using higher-tier materials.
The Mk2 Pumping Module has the ability to run four recipes at a time, each of which runs at the same speed as a Mk1 Pumping Module. Multiple recipes can target the same fluid, meaning that the Mk2 Pumping Module can be as much as four times the speed of a Mk1 if all recipes are for the same fluid, or it can be used to collect many more distinct fluids at the same time. However, it requires SpaceTime to craft, making it more expensive than the other two modules above.
Component Assembly Line
The UIV Component Assembly Line (CoAL) is generally not considered very useful. It requires large amounts of Transcendent Metal, which is very slow to produce before the Godforge, and there are few recipes that specifically require UIV components outside of the Dyson Swarm and Godforge. Because the UMV CoAL is fairly cheap after getting Eternal coils on a DTPF, most players wait to upgrade their CoAL until they can make the UMV casings instead.
Nano Forge and PCB Factory
A Tier 3 PCB Factory with a Thermosink Radiator and Biochamber
The Tier 3 Nano Forge can be built in early UIV by constructing a second addition to the structure and inserting a Transcendent Metal Nanite into the controller. It unlocks a few new Nanites, but the only ones relevant in UIV are Gold Nanites (needed for QFT catalysts and the tier 3 PCB Factory) and Six-Phased Copper Nanites (required for most Godforge modules). It also provides a perfect overclock on all Tier 2 Nanites, which is particularly valuable for the large amount of Glowstone Nanites needed for Optical circuits.
The PCB Factory can be upgraded to Tier 3 after obtaining a Gold Nanite, using a completely new structure. The Tier 3 PCB Factory is similar to the Tier 2, but it gets more circuit boards for the same amount of resources, and uses Gold Nanites instead of Silver Nanites to determine its parallel amount. After obtaining SpaceTime, it can also be upgraded by replacing the Liquid Cooling Tower with the Thermosink Radiator, which allows for perfect overclocks.
Quantum Force Transformer
The Tier 3 Quantum Force Transformer is unlocked with UIV components and a running Tier 2 QFT, and unlocks three new line skips:
- Wetware
- Particles (notably including Unknown Particles and Gravitons)
- Naquadria (also required for the tier 4 QFT)
In addition to QFT progression, the Superconductor Rare-Earth Composite produced from the Monazite QFT is used for the Godforge.
Sidequests
Deep Dark
The Deep Dark is a dimension added by Extra Utilities; it is accessed with the Deep Dark Portal, which is made through Thaumcraft infusion using UIV Field Generators. Its most noteworthy feature is that it contains every ore in the game when mined using a Void Miner , including some ores that are otherwise completely unobtainable, such as Tritanium. It is not immediately required, but some Deep Dark-exclusive ores are needed for progression later on, beginning with Deep Dark Iron at the end of UMV to produce Eternity.
Chaotic Core
The Chaotic Core, which is unlocked with UMV Circuits and SpaceTime, is the final core used in Draconic Evolution crafts. It requires Chaos Shards to make, which can only be obtained at first from a Chaos Guardian, a very powerful boss that spawns on islands in the End that are located at integer multiples of 10,000 on the X and Z axes. Avaritia equipment can be used to improve this method. The first few Chaos Shards can be used to make the Draconic Reactor , which can convert Awakened Draconium Ingots into more Chaos Shards.
The Chaotic Core itself only unlocks a few things. It can be used to make the Chaotic Fusion Casing, the final tier of casing for the DEFC ; this casing does not unlock any new recipes, but does provide a speed boost over the Awakened Draconium Fusion Casing on all recipes. It is used for the Chaotic Capacitor Bank, a source of infinite RF, which has limited uses due to being impossible to convert to EU, but can help with some setups. The Reactor Stabilizer is required for the Draconic Reactor, but is also used in the Singularity Crafting Storage, an infinitely large storage for AE2 Crafting CPUs. In addition, both the Chaotic Capacitor Bank and Singularity Crafting Storage are needed to craft the Stargate .
Uncertainty Resolution
The Uncertainty Resolution is an improved version of the Uncertainty Resolver for Quantum Computers. With the Uncertainty Resolution, the puzzle will be solved instantly as soon as the QC is turned on, and will never spontaneously unsolve, making it especially useful for setting up Dyson Swarms. It requires UIV Field Generators, and therefore is gated behind UMV circuits.
Thaumometric Essentia Cell
The Thaumometric Essentia Cell is a creative cell for essentia. By placing it into an ME Drive, the connected network will have access to infinite essentia of all 69 aspects. It also requires UMV circuits to craft, in addition to some Thaumcraft progression.

documents.text:
Mega Ultimate Voltage (UMV) is the twelfth electric tier in GregTech: New Horizons. Its primary focus is the Eye of Harmony , a multiblock that is extremely expensive both to make and to run, and which is required to progress to the next and final tier, UXV . It is one of the most straightforward tiers in the pack, with very few new technologies outside of its main progression pathway.
The Eye of Harmony, the centerpiece of UMV
Progression
UXV Circuits
By the time the player begins producing UMV components, they should have a DTPF with Eternal coils, providing access to a better SpaceTime recipe, in addition to new materials like Shirabon and UMV Superconductor Base. Shirabon is required to make Quantum Circuits, the only UXV circuit, which are needed to make UMV Field Generators and casings for the Eye of Harmony.
Component Assembly Line
The UMV Component Assembly Line (CoAL) is one of the most useful CoAL tiers, and should be made very early in UMV. It is fairly cheap with an Eternal DTPF for SpaceTime and Hypogen, and provides a discount on the large amount of UMV components needed for Wireless Energy Hatches and the Eye of Harmony. It also covers any skipped lower tier CoALs, and doubles the speed of all lower tier components.
Eye of Harmony
See More: Eye of Harmony
The Eye of Harmony (EoH) is the center of UMV progression. It is a very expensive multiblock that is able to produce almost every dust in the game, largely replacing Space Elevator Miners and Void Miners , as well as all the plasmas used for Exotic Catalyst, but its main use is making the four materials that cannot be produced in any other way: White Dwarf Matter, Black Dwarf Matter, Universium, and Stellar Plasma. Stellar Plasma is produced by all EoH recipes, and is primarily used for the top tier DTPF catalyst, making various UXV materials, and running parallels in the EoH, and is also usable as fuel for the Godforge. White Dwarf Matter is only produced by tier 1-tier 3 recipes, and is mainly used in tier 2-tier 4 casings. Black Dwarf Matter is similar: it is only produced by tier 4-tier 6 recipes, and mainly used in tier 5-tier 7 casings. Universium is produced by tier 7-tier 9 recipes, and is required for tier 8-tier 9 casings, but its main use is UXV components, which demand very large amounts of it.
Climbing the tiers of the Eye of Harmony is necessary to finish UMV. The EoH has three different types of casings: spacetime compression field generators, which determine maximum recipe tier, time dilation field generators, which increase speed, and stabilisation field generators, which increase recipe success chance. Determining the best order to upgrade them is complex, but one example is listed on the Eye of Harmony's wiki page. At base speed, the EoH is incredibly slow, encouraging players to overclock it. However, the EoH has inefficient overclocks compared to most other machines (taking 8x the EU/t for 2x the speed, as compared to 4x for most machines), forcing players who want to overclock the EoH to expand their power production first. Although only a 7/x/x EoH is strictly needed to start UXV, its Universium production is unusably slow for any serious UXV crafts; a 9/9/9 EoH with Astral Arrays for parallels will be needed before UXV components become easily affordable.
Stellar Catalyst
Stellar catalyst is the fifth and final tier of DTPF catalyst, made from Stellar Plasma. Unlike the first four tiers, all of which require only plasmas that can be made in a Fusion Reactor Mk3, Stellar catalyst requires two Mk5 recipes (for Lead and Thorium Plasma) and a Plasma Fabricator recipe (for Naquadria Plasma), in addition to the Stellar Plasma. Many low-tier DTPF recipes, such as Neutronium or LuV-UV Superconductor Base, do not have Stellar catalyst variants, meaning Exotic catalyst remains useful even after Stellar catalyst can be produced in bulk. However, some materials, such as Hypogen and UHV+ Superconductor Base, do have improved Stellar variants, and Stellar catalyst is the only catalyst accepted for a few recipes, such as the direct Tesseract to Transcendent Metal recipe.
Godforge Upgrades
See More: Forge of the Gods
The Forge of the Gods (Godforge), which was optional in UIV, is required by the end of UMV in order to produce Magmatter, which is needed for all UXV components.
Producing Magmatter requires the END upgrade, the final upgrade in the Godforge's upgrade tree, which needs a minimum of 84 Graviton Shards to reach if all optional upgrades are skipped. 99 Graviton Shards are obtainable before the END upgrade, since the last two steps in the Composition milestone both require it, meaning that only 15 Graviton Shards can go uncollected. This can be done in one of two main ways: by skipping the tier 7 on two of the three available milestones, or by skipping both the tier 6 and tier 7 on one of the three milestones. In both cases, all of the other milestones must be completed up to tier 7. Another option is to avoid making the second ring, leaving Composition at tier 4, and only have one other milestone below tier 7. The following table lists the requirements for each of these skippable milestones.
Milestone | Requirement (Tier 6) | Requirement (Tier 7)
Charge | 5.9e19 EU | 5.31e20 EU
Conversion | 10.24 billion recipes | 40.96 billion recipes
Catalyst | 2.43 million Fuel Units | 7.29 million Fuel Units
Catalyst is mainly progressed by using a high Fuel Consumption Factor (especially after the TSE upgrade) over a long time, and using higher tier fuels for the Godforge: Dimensionally Transcendent Residue has very punishing exponential scaling, while Stellar Plasma has less punishing exponential scaling and Magnetohydrodynamically Constrained Star Matter scales linearly, although the latter is not practical until UXV. Charge and Conversion can both be progressed by running as many recipes as possible, with the former benefiting from the TBF upgrade and the latter from anything that increases parallels.
Both of these routes will leave at least one Graviton Shard left over after completing the END upgrade. Combined with the 6 Graviton Shards that can be immediately obtained from placing a Heliofusion Exoticizer in Magmatter mode, it is possible to get the TPTP upgrade even if the player did not originally go down the right path in the upgrade tree's split. This upgrade is necessary for producing Magmatter, since some of the plasmas that the recipe can request are multi-step, and can only be made in the Plasma Fabricator.
In addition to Graviton Shards, many of the upgrades also require items to be inserted to complete them. The most notable costs are the Eternity and Universium needed for the last two upgrades, forcing them to be unlocked only after a tier 7 Eye of Harmony, and the 24 total UMV batteries required for all of the upgrades.
Infrastructure
Power
The Eye of Harmony is extremely power-hungry, and will likely consume most of the player's power generation while they progress through its tiers. Without any overclocks its power usage is fairly modest, on the order of 100B EU/t, but it is also extremely slow, and adding even a single overclock increases it to multiple trillion EU/t due to its very inefficient overclocks. In UMV, there are three viable sources of power to run the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure.
Dyson Swarm
See More: Dyson Swarm Ground Unit
Dyson Swarm Ground Units (Dysons) remain viable in UMV to power the Eye of Harmony and its supporting infrastructure, although unlike Antimatter or power EoHs, they cannot scale through UXV. The Matter Manipulator is very useful for placing large numbers of Dysons and their supporting Quantum Computers , and the Energized Wireless Dynamo Hatch can be used to avoid placing Lapotronic Supercapacitors . Completing UMV comfortably with Dysons typically requires dozens of them, and completing the tier quickly can take hundreds.
Naquadah Fuel
See More: Naquadah Fuel Refinery and Large Naquadah Reactor
Naqfuel in UMV should be built with an eye towards using depleted Naq5 or Naq6 in the SSASS , although in UMV power demands can be low enough to still rely only on the Large Naquadah Reactor . UMV also unlocks the final upgrades to Naqfuel, with Tier 4 coils for the Naquadah Fuel Refinery allowing all recipes, including a single-step recipe for Naq4, as well as the ability to make Naq6 using Shirabon and optionally Stellar Plasma. The Energized Wireless Dynamo Hatch can also be used to simplify the logistics of getting power out of Large Naquadah Reactor arrays.
Antimatter
See More: Semi-Stable Antimatter Stabilization Sequencer and Shielded Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix
The SSASS, the multiblock used to produce Antimatter
Antimatter becomes much more powerful in UMV, thanks to the tier unlocking much better additives for the Semi-Stable Antimatter Stabilization Sequencer that allow for each one to produce over 100T EU/t when properly supplied. In early UMV, these additives are Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid, Spatially Enlarged Fluid, Molten Shirabon, and depleted Naq6, which can produce nearly 60T EU/t per SSASS. Later in the tier, Molten Eternity can be used to more than double this number. The Stabilized Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix can now use UMV Superconductor Base as its matter, which increases the net EU/t produced by as much as 24% and allows it to output directly to the wireless network.
Power Eye of Harmony
The second viable method of endgame power generation is the power-generating Eye of Harmony. After improving an EoH to 7/7/7 or better, it becomes net-positive on power as long as it does not run any overclocks or parallels. Power-generating EoHs can produce a maximum of 12.87T EU/t when running the T10 Deep Dark recipe with 9/9/9 casings, meaning that reaching the Stargate typically requires at least a hundred of them.
Wireless Energy
UMV adds many new hatches for working with wireless energy, capable of replacing non-wireless energy for everything except multiblocks that need laser hatches. UXV circuits unlock UIV and UMV Wireless Energy Hatches, meaning that unlike in UIV, it is possible to use wireless for on-tier power. In addition, Shirabon unlocks multi-amp (although not laser) Wireless Energy Hatches, which are helpful for multiblocks like the Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver or Quantum Computer , that accept multi-amp hatches and either don't accept or don't need laser hatches. The UMV Capacitor can also be used to download up to 10P EU/t to a Lapotronic Supercapacitor , for any multiblocks that need enough energy from laser hatches that the UIV Capacitor is insufficient.
UMV also introduces the only wireless Dynamo Hatch, the Energized Wireless Dynamo Hatch, which can be used on Dyson Swarm Ground Units or Large Naquadah Reactors (although not the Stabilized Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix ) and can output up to 65,536 amps of UMV (approximately 8.8T EU/t) directly to the wireless network. Crafting it requires an Eye of Harmony, as the recipe uses Stellar Catalyst.
Dimensional Convergence
See More: DTPF#Dimensional Convergence
Dimensional Convergence is a mechanic that can be used to gain perfect overclocks for the DTPF , at the cost of increased catalyst consumption. It is unlocked in UMV, requiring UMV Energy Hatches and Field Generators to make the Transdimensional Alignment Matrix that is used to activate it in a DTPF. Although convergence is never required, it is very useful for avoiding DTPF spam or immense power consumption in the endgame. However, because it requires a full catalyst discount to run, using convergence demands the ability to run a DTPF passively with 100% uptime, including the increased speed and catalyst usage of convergence. An Eye of Harmony running the Deep Dark recipe can help with this, as that recipe produces all 16 plasmas used for Exotic Catalyst.
Machine Scaling
Building the Eye of Harmony requires robust on-demand crafting infrastructure, especially for its higher tier casings. In order to bring the crafting time for Eye of Harmony parts to a reasonable level, UMV demands players to scale their arrays of standard on-demand machines, such as Industrial Cutting Factories and Fluid Shapers . The Matter Manipulator is highly recommended for doing this. Priority rotation between Crafting Input Proxies can be used to reduce the risk of bottlenecks on these machines.
Advanced Assembly Lines (AALs) are particularly important to scale, because of how slow the recipes for EoH casings are. Before overclocking, tier 1 casings take 4000 seconds, or 66 minutes, to craft, and each tier adds another 4000 seconds to the recipe time, up to 36000 seconds, or 10 hours, for tier 9 casings. Many of the ingredients in their recipes also require the Assembly Line, including very large quantities of high-tier circuits. This demand can be handled either by making dedicated AALs for each of the slow recipes or by scaling universal AALs, but in either case it is necessary to build more AALs and supply them with more power.
Wireless Computation
Shirabon also unlocks the Cloud Computation Client Hatch and Cloud Computation Server Hatch, which can be used to transfer computation wirelessly between Quantum Computers , Network Switches , and computation-using multiblocks such as the Research Station . Like wireless Assembly Line data, wireless computation is many-to-many, unlike its wired equivalent, which is one-to-one.
Space Elevator
UMV unlocks two Space Elevator upgrades, although both require Universium and as such are late in the tier. The first is the Mk5 motor, the highest tier, which unlocks all 24 module slots and is required for the Mk3 Space Assembler module. The second is the Mk3 pumping module, which is 16 times as fast as the Mk2 version, while retaining its ability to run 4 recipes at once.
Quantum Force Transformer
The tier 4 Quantum Force Transformer is unlocked with UMV components and a running Tier 3 QFT, and unlocks three new line skips immediately:
- Radox/Kevlar
- Bio Catalyst/Mutated Living Solder
- Seaweed
The Radox skip is especially valuable, due to how slow the standard Radox recipe is and how much is needed for UMV and UXV circuits, although making a tier 4 QFT requires over 1.6 ML of Radox first. The Bio Catalyst recipe is also very useful, and these two recipes combined should make the tier 4 QFT a priority upon entering UMV.
It is also required to run the Eternity loop after reaching a Tier 7 Eye of Harmony, and for the Z Boson, Lambda, and Omega particle recipe that is needed for the Stargate .
Sidequests
Giga Chad Token
The Giga Chad Token is an item that can be made in UMV to complete a quest and for bragging rights, and is otherwise only used in the Stargate . It requires a stack of UEV, UIV, and UMV Field Generators, 100ML of Exotic Catalyst, and some SpaceTime in the DTPF , and takes 48 hours to craft without any overclocks.
Old Stargate
UMV contains the third old Stargate trophy, the Stargate of Dimensional Duplicity, corresponding to version 2.2.3. This old Stargate is very expensive on UMV circuits and components, in addition to many of the components used in previous old Stargates: it requires 167k Bio Mainframes and 21M UHV Superconductor, like the UEV old Stargate, but also takes 820ML of SpaceTime, 142k Pico Circuits, and 65k UMV Motors. It also, like the UEV Stargate, requires Assembly Line recipes that are both very slow and need UXV power, meaning they cannot be run in the Advanced Assembly Line until the next tier.

documents.text:
Welcome to Extended Mega Ultimate Voltage (UXV) the thirteenth and final tier in GregTech: New Horizons. This tier begins with the production of Magnetohydrodynamically Constrained Star Matter (MHDCSM) and ends with a Stargate . In UXV, expect to spam even more machines and drastically increase power production to support laser energy hatches.
Tier Walkthrough
1) Eternity and MHDCSM
The end feels near after finally reaching a 7/7/7 EOH and holding universium for the first time. Unfortunately, UXV components and a 9/9/9 EOH are still a long ways off. Tipler and Gallifreyan EOH parts are crafted with MHDCSM bolts which require a new material, eternity, and many universium nanites .
Eternity is actually very cheap to manufacture in the QFT , but it has a steep up-front cost. The recipe requires the Temporal Harmonizer Catalyst and a Chronic Singularity which take 20,736L of universium combined. Once complete, however, the catalyst lasts forever and the player no longer needs universium to craft additional Chronic Singularities. Note that eternity only has a 25% chance of being produced and should absolutely be focused with fermium and neptunium plasma to nearly triple the probability of success to 72%. Good luck.
The first available recipe for MHDCSM is also very expensive and the player should switch to the cheaper version using eternity nanites as soon as possible. It reduces the universium cost by 50% and does not require any BDM or WDM. Unfortunately, the cheaper recipe is rated at MAX voltage which means the player needs a 4A UXV energy hatch to overclock their EIC . That is another up-front cost totaling 21,888L of universium, and needs the END upgrade in the Godforge. See the table below for a quick cost breakdown.
In order to obtain enough universium for just these three components, a player needs their 7/7/7 EOH to succeed 53 times. On average, that takes 135 iterations or 111.2 hours assuming no overclocks, 70% yield, 39.5% probability of success, and a recipe length of 2,965 seconds. It is highly recommended to build a second or even third 7/7/7 EOH to cut this time down significantly. Also try using antimatter for power to overclock the EOH as much as possible.
Components | High-Level Cost Breakdown | Low-Level Cost Breakdown | Leftover
1 Temporal Harmonizer Catalyst 1 Chronic Singularity 1 UXV Energy Hatch | 2 Timepieces 1 Universium Nanite 10,704L MHDCSM 1,152L Universium | 42,624L Universium 20,736L WDM 20,736L BDM | 1 Timepiece 1 Universium Nanite 816L MHDCSM
2) END upgrade of Godforge
All UXV components require Magmatter, which is unlocked by the END upgrade of the Forge of the Gods . The production of Magmatter is relatively cheap, but the final two upgrades are expensive, requiring (among other components) 22 Mega Ultimate Batteries.
3) Finish EOH Progression
A complete 9/9/9 Eye of Harmony (EOH).
Players may proceed towards a 9/9/9 EOH once they have access to eternity. Recall that compression field generators offer the largest increase to star matter production and should be prioritized first, then time dilation field generators, and finally stabilisation field generators. Additional 9/9/9 EOHs are much easier after the first one. Don't forget to replace any UMV input hatches with humongous input hatches and use the T10 Deep Dark planet recipe because that provides the most resources out of all the planets.
The player can then begin splitting their EOHs between production and power. Expect only 3-4 EOHs for producing raw stellar plasma, WDM, BDM, and universium. This is because production EOHs use astral arrays (AA) to run parallels within the same machine. Ensure that there is enough power and raw stellar plasma to support even a single AA before investing in one, but know that they are extremely powerful and quickly ease the pain of producing universium. The first one, for example, costs the equivalent of one 9/9/9 EOH but acts as seven! For universium, leave the EOH at 9/8/9 to keep stellar plasma production net positive.
An EOH running T0 Overworld with one or two AAs is very effective at mass producing raw stellar plasma. This is a reasonable time to switch to excited dimensionally transcendent stellar catalyst exclusively for all DTPF recipes that allow it. Not only does that increase the speed and efficiency of producing expensive materials such as superconductors and hypogen, but it drastically reduces the need for plasma (especially when combined with the immense amount of plasma produced by EOHs). However, this consumes quite a lot of power which may not be fully sustainable right-away.
An EOH running T10 Deep Dark with many AAs is very effective at mass producing spacetime. It is safe to turn off any DTPFs producing it--they simply cannot compete with the speed or efficiency of the EOH. For reference, a single failed recipe outputs 7.3M (L) of spacetime. This is also a reasonable time to switch over to spacetime for superconductor wire recipes if that is still a bottleneck for any PrASS .
4) UXV Upgrades
Much like the previous tiers, the player should acquire CoAL casings before mass producing UXV components. The 25% discount saves the player a massive amount of universium, but comes with yet another steep up-front cost. A full set of 43 UXV CoAL casings cost 27.5M (L) of universium, 161k (L) of BDM, and 265M (L) of raw stellar plasma, among other things.
A fully-upgraded Forge of the Gods
After acquiring UXV CoAL casings, the player may be interested in wireless laser energy hatches for multiblocks including but not limited to the CoAL , QFT , DTPF , Nano Forge , PCB Factory , Advanced Assembly Line , Exothermic Hearth , Endothermic Fridge , Mega Alloy Blast Smelter , Space Elevator , and Research Station . The ability to transfer more than 64A wirelessly means LSCs are no longer necessary to have all around your base and neither are the capacitors within them.
An operational Stargate.
The player may also be interested in Space Assembler Module MK-IIIs which unlock the artificial universe ME storage cell and the ME fluid artificial universe storage cell. These have the same capacity as their digital singularity equivalents, but allow more than one type. The Space Assembler Module MK-IIIs also help significantly with the production of optical circuit components because they run at UXV with 64 parallels which is much faster than MK-IIs running at UIV with 16 parallels.
Lastly, make the final upgrade to the Forge of the Gods which includes a third ring for four additional module slots and allows the player to follow all three split paths of the upgrade tree.
5) The Door to Heaven
This is it. The only real thing left to do is go forth and craft a Stargate . It will not be easy and may take days, if not weeks, to complete. Before getting started, delete all redundant infrastructure to save as much TPS as possible and switch to the most efficient recipes (ie. UMV superconductors for opticals) where possible.
The full list of required materials is extensive, but know that one stargate costs 1.21B (L) of universium, 35.6B (L) of spacetime, 9.16B (L) of hypogen, 160B (L) of infinity, 699M (L) of Magmatter, 464M transcendent metal, 1.16M quantum circuits, and 3.46M pico circuits. It is highly recommended to pre-craft a few components such as the quantum/pico circuits (or go outside and touch some grass) while waiting on the universium. Don't forget to take screenshots of your base and post them in the #screenshot-brag channel on the Discord!
Tips & Tricks
EOH Handling
If not done so already, the player should absolutely automate their EOHs. Visit the EOH wiki page for an in-depth walkthrough on that process and everything else regarding the multiblock. Note that the humongous input hatch allows the player to use the shortcut method for filling power EOHs which heavily simplifies their automation and reduces idle time.
Graviton Shards
The Stargate requires 512 Graviton Shards, which can be ejected from the Godforge after completing its final upgrade, END. After unlocking Inversion by reaching level 7 on each milestone, it becomes possible to scale the milestones infinitely to produce enough shards. Each of the four milestones can be pushed in order to rapidly gain shards, although it is more efficient to prioritize one or two milestones due to the fact that the number of shards gained scales quadratically, while the requirements only scale linearly. Charge can be pushed by using the unlimited maximum voltage unlocked by the TBF upgrade, Conversion by running a cheap recipe such as steel and re-macerating it repeatedly, Catalyst by using MHDCSM with a high fuel factor, and Composition by placing more Heliofusion Exoticizers in Magmatter mode.
Saving TPS
TPS is likely a massive issue at this point in the game. No one wants to run their game at half-speed, especially while waiting tens of hours for enough universium to progress. Try using Spark, Lag Goggles, or another performance profiler to identify anything that may be causing unnecessary performance issues.

The Energy Unit (EU) is GregTech's unit of electrical energy. EU is used to run GregTech and IC2 machines. Every Tier offers multiple types of Power Generation options at LV and above. EU is also compatible with machines from Applied Energistics 2 and other machines that accept Redstone Flux (RF), converting at a rate of 1 EU to 3.6 RF. The reverse is not possible; RF cannot be converted to EU.
Voltage and Amperage

Acronym: LV | Voltage Tier: Low Voltage | EU Limit: 32

EU in GregTech comes in a system of Voltage (Volts, V) and Amperage (Amps, A).
Energy is transferred in packages. Voltage describes the size of the energy packages, while Amperage describes the number of packages. When you multiply both, you get the power in EU/t (Energy Units per tick), which describes the energy produced, transferred, or consumed over time.
Quick Tip
- If you have X generators of Tier Y, use cables that can handle X Amperes of Tier Y.
Voltage Tiers
Main Article: Tier
GregTech uses voltage tiers to define its progression. The voltage of a Generator (or, for a multiblock generator, its Dynamo Hatch) determines the maximum amount of EU it can generate and transfer per amp. The voltage of a single-block machine or Energy Hatch determines the maximum EU that can be present in any given amp before the machine explodes. The minimum voltage required to process a recipe is listed next to the usage or voltage in NEI .
The EU Limit of each subsequent tier is typically four times the previous.
Note: When used as numbers in calculations, the ULV Tier counts as Tier 0, the LV Tier counts as Tier 1, and so on.
Amperage
In code, amps are pushed, not pulled. However, they are only pushed when requested by machines. Thus, for all scopes except pack development, you can assume amps are only ever pulled as needed.
Machines and energy hatches draw amps to fill their internal EU buffers. The capacity of the internal buffer is listed as "Capacity:" in the machine's or hatch's tooltip. When processing a recipe, a machine will draw from its internal buffer. The current contents of the internal buffer can be checked with the Portable Scanner .
The maximum amount of amps a machine can draw is either listed on its tooltip or recipe-dependent. A machine can draw up to a maximum of ⌊ 2 × Recipe Usage EU/t Voltage Tier EU Limit ⌋ + 1 {\displaystyle {\displaystyle \left\lfloor {\frac {2\times {\text{Recipe Usage EU/t}}}{\text{Voltage Tier EU Limit}}}\right\rfloor +1}} amps to fill its internal buffer. This means that if the machine isn't processing a recipe, it will draw 1 amp to refill the internal buffer. Recipe amperages listed in NEI are a recommended number to fill the internal buffer at a rate that breaks even against usage.
Several common amperages of GregTech machines can be found in the table below. "Drawing" means "draws up to", unless otherwise stated.
Output amps contain the maximum EU for the outputting machine's voltage tier.
Machine | Notes
Machine: Singleblock Generators | Notes: Output 1A of its tier
Machine: Energy Hatches | Notes: Draws 2A (second amp mostly for extra draw for loss)
Machine: Step-up Transformers | Notes: Draws 4A lower voltage, outputs 1A higher voltage
Machine: Step-down Transformers | Notes: Draws 1A higher voltage, outputs 4A lower voltage
Machine: Battery Buffers | Notes: Draws 2A per Battery, outputs 1A per Battery.
Machine: Battery Chargers | Notes: Draws 4-8A per Battery, outputs 2-4A per Battery correspondingly.
Machine: Arc Furnace | Notes: Most recipes require 3A to break even against EU/t usage
Machine: Thermal Centrifuge | Notes: Most recipes require 2A to break even against EU/t usage
Overclocking
Main Article: Overclocking
Machines of higher tiers can receive overclocks to speed up their recipes.
Regular overclocks double the recipe's speed and total EU consumption, leading to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, overclocking is also called 2/4 overclocking.
A perfect overclock instead quadruples the recipe's speed while keeping the total EU consumption the same. This still leads to quadrupled EU/t usage. For this reason, perfect overclocking is also called 4/4 overclocking.
Machines typically receive one overclock per voltage tier above the minimum required for a recipe.
Singleblock machines can only ever regular overclock.
Multiblock machines perfect overclock on a case-by-case basis; their tooltips contain information on how to achieve perfect overclocks or upgrade overclocks to perfect overclocks. If no information is mentioned, they will regular overclock.
Multiblocks with two energy hatches of the same voltage will always draw 4A to overclock a recipe to a tier higher than the energy hatch voltage (since 4A of the lower voltage contains the same EU as 1A of the higher voltage). This also allows them to run recipes with a minimum requirement of that higher voltage tier.
Cables and Loss
GregTech EU can be transferred using GregTech Cables.
Rather than priority by destination, power priority is given by cardinal direction. Cables will push power in the following priority:
- Down
- Up
- North
- South
- West
- East
When producing power, each generator will always attempt to empty all of its internal buffer at once. This can cause one generator in a cable network to use fuel more rapidly than another, with order depending on tile entity processing and changing on chunk reloads.
All GT Cables have a max Voltage, max Amperage and a Loss/Meter/Ampere, indicated on their tooltip:
- Cables which receive amps containing more EU than their maximum Voltage will catch fire and melt.
- Cables that have more amps travelling through them than their maximum Amperage limit will catch fire and melt. Note that machines can request more Amperage than strictly required by their active recipe.
- Each energy packet travelling through a cable loses Voltage per block travelled. The amount of EU lost is indicated by the Loss/Meter/Ampere number.
Each Material has 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x uninsulated Wires. Most of these have cable variants, except for the superconductor wires, as well as graphene, Ichorium, hypogen, Black Plutonium, Awakened Draconium, Infinity, and SpaceTime wires. Note that Uninsulated Wires have twice the Loss/Meter/Ampere as Insulated Cables. The only exceptions to this are Red alloy and Redstone alloy (as their cables are lossless, while the wires are not), Quantium, Lumiium, and Signalium (four times the loss when uninsulated), and Bedrockium (8x loss when uninsulated).
For example:
- A 1x Tin Cable can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 1 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. This means that 1 amp can travel 32 blocks before it dies.
- A 1x Tin Wire can handle 1A containing 32EU at a loss of 2 EU-Volt/Meter/Ampere. In this case, the amp can travel 16 blocks only.

Multi-Amp Generation
Multiblock Generators use Dynamo Hatches to output power. These come in 1A, 4A, 16A, and 64A variants. These generators will always attempt to fill existing generated amps with EU before generating more amps.
Output Loss
Any GT Block outputting EU has an energy loss on output. This means there is no such thing as lossless power transfer. A power outputting singleblock will take 8 × 4 t i e r + 2 m a x ( 0 , t i e r − 1 ) {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 8\times 4^{tier}+2^{max(0,tier-1)}}} EU from its internal buffer and output 8 × 4 t i e r {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 8\times 4^{tier}}} EU (which is always the maximum EU one amp of that voltage tier can hold). For example, a LV Combustion Generator draws 33 EU from its internal buffer to generate 1 amp holding 32 EU. The energy lost is therefore 2 m a x ( 0 , t i e r − 1 ) {\displaystyle {\displaystyle 2^{max(0,tier-1)}}} .

Transformers
Picture of a Transformer in default mode transferring 1 amp of HV into 4 amps of MV.
Transformers convert EU between voltage tiers. In Step Up mode, they draw up to 4 amps of a lower voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce 1A of a higher voltage. This can allow lower tier amps to power higher tier machines which may only draw 1-2 A for a recipe. Similarly, in Step Down mode, they draw 1 amp of a higher voltage to fill their internal buffers, and draw from their internal buffers to produce up to 4A of a lower voltage. This allows use of higher tier power generators with lower tier machines while preventing explosions. Use a Soft Mallet to switch the mode.
The big dot with a plus is the high voltage side and is the front face, while the five smaller circles are the lower voltage sides. Regardless of mode, the big dot is always for the higher voltage. That means in Step Up mode, transformers have one output, five inputs, and in Step Down mode, they have five outputs, one input.
The output loss section above applies to transformer outputs as well.
Power Transformer and Hi-Amp Transformer
The Power Transformer and the Hi-Amp Transformer work like an ordinary transformer with one exception:
The Hi-Amp Transformer will accept 4 amps of higher voltage and turn it into 16 amps of lower voltage in its default mode. In inverted mode it will transform 16amps lower voltage to 4 amps of higher voltage.
The Power Transformer will accept 16 amps of higher voltage and turn it into 64 amps of lower voltage in its default mode. In inverted mode it will transform 64 amps lower voltage to 16 amps of higher voltage.
Active Transformer
The Active Transformer is a multiblock unlocked in ZPM tier that can transform to and from any voltage, accepting energy with an Energy Hatch and outputting energy with a Dynamo Hatch.
- Note: Prior to Version 2.7.0 Wrenching or modifying the Active Transformer while it is running would cause it to explode.
Trivia
- GregTech's current power system is called the GT Enet API (Enet).
- Since version 5.0 (for Minecraft 1.7.2), GregTech has its own Energy System since GregoriusT wasn't satisfied with IC2 Experimental's Energy System.
The reasons of why I removed compatibility to the IC² Enet are that Cable Loss doesn't work, that the Network doesn't have Packets anymore and that it switched from Integer to Double (what is horrible for larger Energy Storages). Not to mention that it is very hard to have control over Energy flow without constantly registering and unregistering TileEntities. — GregoriusT

documents.text:
Power Generation is a core concept of GTNH, necessary at every tier beyond the Stone Age . There are many different options, available and useful at varying points of progression. So many options are available that it may be confusing to new players. This page lists many of the most viable power generation options, what tiers they are available and useful at, and how to use them.
Steam
Steam is the first power source you have access to, and is the fuel for the first Bronze and Steel machines. Upon reaching LV , it is also the easiest way to generate EU, but boilers rapidly become less useful in the following tiers due to how difficult it becomes to transport a lot of Steam around to match the EU/t demands of your upgraded machines, especially your Electric Blast Furnace. After players centralise their power generation (usually around EV - IV) and no longer need to transport "fuel" around their base, Steam starts to become increasingly useful in power generation again, especially as they gain access to superheated, supercritical or dense variants of Steam.
Production
Single-Block Boilers
Steam is produced in boilers ; all boilers require 1L of water per 160L of steam produced. If a boiler is fed water while it is still hot, it will explode , so ensure you've got enough water production for your boilers!
These are the initial single-block boilers from GregTech:
- The Small Coal Boiler is the first boiler available, consuming coal or charcoal, and is not really viable for electricity production, giving a measly 120 L/s of steam, or 3 EU/t of power, or even less with efficiency losses from turbines.
- The High Pressure Coal Boiler produces 300 L/s of steam (equivalent to 7.5 EU/t). Like the Small Coal Boilers, these run off coal or charcoal. You typically need 3-5 of these to power a single Low Voltage Machine constantly.
- The Simple Solar Boiler produces the same amount of steam as a Small Coal Boiler, but runs off sunlight. It slowly calcifies over time, requiring it to be broken and replaced to be restored to its full 120 L/s production. To prevent calcification, Distilled Water can be used instead of normal water, which is uneconomical without a Distillation Tower at HV .
- The High Pressure Solar Boiler is an upgraded version of the Simple Solar, producing 360L/s at full power. It calcifies in the same way as the Simple Solar Boiler, but will never go below 120L/s. It can be restored to full capacity by breaking and replacing when it starts to lose production. Solar panels have a high initial crafting cost to account for making power passively for setups that use small amounts of power, constantly.
- The High Pressure Lava Boiler produces 600 L/s of steam, or 15 EU/t, and runs off lava. These require a constant source of lava, which is generally not something available at LV. This makes it so that they are not recommended for use in constant power generation. They have a multiblock upgrade in EV tier, the Large Heat Exchanger, which proves a lot more useful.
- GT++ Advanced Boilers are single-block machines available in 3 tiers, from LV to HV which produce 750L/s, 1500 L/s, and 2250L/s respectively.
Multi-Block Boilers
- Railcraft Boilers , must have a 1x1, 2x2, or 3x3 base, and can be up to 5 blocks tall. They consist of a single base layer of Boiler Fireboxes, with up to 4 layers of boiler tanks on top. The boiler fireboxes determine what fuel is used- Solid Fueled Fireboxes can run on anything that is capable of burning in a furnace, (e.g. Charcoal), while Liquid Fueled Fireboxes run off certain flammable liquids (Creosote Oil, Lava and Oil, though of these the only one you'll want to use is probably Creosote). The boiler tanks determine Steam production, warm up time, and fuel consumption- low pressure Boilers warm up faster (although still very slow relative to other boilers) and make 10 L/t of steam per boiler tank present(Note that this is per tick, not per second unlike the GT boilers- multiply this by 20 to get per second), while high pressure Boilers are more expensive, use twice the fuel, warm up much slower, but make 40L/t of steam per boiler tank. Both types of fireboxes are viable, and it's generally best to run a combination of both to fully utilize a coke oven. These can produce anywhere from a tiny 10L/t of steam, or 5 EU/t, up to 360L/t for a max size low pressure or 1440L/t for a max size high pressure (180 or 720 EU/t, respectively). The fuel consumption uses a complicated formula; more details here .
- GregTech's Large Boilers ; the Large Bronze Boiler is available at late LV (as soon as you have MV circuits) and the Large Steel Boiler is available shortly after. These burn (extremely large quantities of) any furnace fuel or flammable liquid. Running these off Creosote Oil is very difficult due to the large amounts required (starting at 625L/s). These produce enormous amounts of Steam, 19,200L/s (480 EU/t) for a Bronze and 1,200 EU/t for a Steel Boiler. Eventually (HV and EV) there are Titanium and Tungstensteel Large Boilers available that can burn more advanced fuels like Cetane Boosted Diesel and High Octane Gasoline to produce Superheated Steam, which can be more efficient than using a generator.
Later Tier Steam Production
In later tiers, large quantities of Supercritical or Superheated Steam can be produced by a Large Heat Exchanger fed by hot fluids like lava or hot coolant, which is able to be produced infinitely in several ways (e.g Everburn Urns from Thaumcraft). Another way to get Superheated Steam is through the Large Titanium Boiler and Large Tungstensteel Boiler, but run only with more specific fuels (like Solid Super Fuels). This continues into the endgame, with Dense Supercritical Steam being provided by an Extreme Heat Exchanger . Many mid- to late-game power generation options use steam in some capacity, whether directly, or via a heat exchanger (e.g. the Fusion Reactor , Solar Tower Fluid Reactors , DEHP , Solid-Oxide Fuel Cells , HTGR , LFTR , THTR ).
Consumption
In the Steam Age, steam machines consume steam directly - converting 2L of Steam into 1EU at 100% efficiency. As you gain access to steam turbines, some will be more or less efficient (e.g. the Basic Steam Turbine is 85% efficient, and so converts 77.6L of Steam into 32 EU, instead of the usual 64L).
Steam is consumed in Steam Turbines - in either single-block or multi-block turbines. Remember that each steam turbine has an efficiency percentage, which will affect the EU/t values listed above. Multi-block turbines like the Large Steam Turbine or the XL Turbo Steam Turbine and their variants can have efficiency ratings above 100%. Many late-game energy setups wll use XLST's with huge rotors, able to process millions of steam per tick.
Oil
Oil is the most common fuel used LV-HV. It's available mid-LV, and is viable until LuV for power generation and useful for other resources far beyond that. Oil itself is not recommended to be used as a fuel, instead it must be refined. The four main fuels obtained from oil, in order of complexity, are light fuel, diesel, cetane-boosted diesel, and high-octane gasoline. Each one is more oil-efficient, complex, and a higher tier than the last. Oil can also be distilled into various useful chemicals- ethylene for polyethylene, a plastic, toluene for explosives, etc. , but this guide is focusing on energy production.
Production: Oil is pumped out of the ground through either pumps on physical oil wells, or oil drilling rigs on bedrock. It is then refined through a process of distillation and refining into four "base" fuels. From there, these base fuels can be cracked, distilled, refined, and mixed into various more complex hydrocarbons or burned directly.
Pumping: There are physical geysers of oil that spawn on the surface. A pump placed on top of these will bring up the oil, which sits in an underground reservoir, when it is fed power and mining pipes. Oil drilling rigs, first available in MV, extract oil from hidden reservoirs under the bedrock, which can be found using prospector's scanners or a seismic prospector.
Distillation and refining: Oil can then be distilled into four primary distillates, in various fractions based on what type of oil it is. A distillery lets you pick one of the four fractions, while a distillation tower creates all four at once. Once the oil has been turned into a fraction, the fraction must be de-sulfurized by mixing it with hydrogen(can be easily obtained by electrolyzing water) in a chemical reactor. The four fractions are light fuel, heavy fuel, naphtha, and refinery gas. Until you obtain a distillation tower, the only two you need to worry about for power generation are light fuel and heavy fuel.
Tiers of Fuel:
- Light fuel is available at LV as a direct product of oil desulfurization.
- Diesel is available at MV from mixing light fuel and heavy fuel in a 5:1 ratio.
- CBD (cetane boosted diesel) is available at HV from mixing diesel with tetranitromethane (made using nitric acid and ethenone in a chemical reactor).
- HOG (high-octane gasoline) is available at HV in a large chemical reactor with EV power from an extremely complex set of recipes (regular gasoline can be made at HV but isn't worth using). It is not a direct upgrade from CBD, rather it gets it's own processing chain.
Each tier is more complex than the last, but more oil-efficient. Light fuel is still a viable source of power even at EV, but at that point making cetane-boosted diesel will triple your power output per cell. Once you obtain a distillation tower, the naphtha and refinery gas can be steam-cracked or hydro-cracked to obtain more light fuel or heavy fuel, or made into various chemicals for use in other applications.
CBD can be used until LuV, but a significant amount of large combustion engines need to be built to use CBD beyond IV. Note that only HOG can be burned in the ECE (extreme combustion engine, the IV multiblock combustion generator that produces 1A of LuV when boosted), which allows oil to be used until late LuV/early ZPM.
Used in: Combustion Generators
Bio Diesel
Bio diesel is a renewable combustion generator fuel made primarily from plants. It has three ingredients and, like regular diesel, can be cetane-boosted for better efficiency. It can be made in LV , but most methods of farming it in decent quantities require MV .
Production: Bio diesel is made out of seed oil or fish oil, ethanol or methanol, and sodium hydroxide.
Seed oil can be obtained from most plants, but the best candidates are peanuts or sesame seeds from Pam's Harvestcraft, or hazelnuts from Extra Trees(Forestry addon). The best ways to farm these are generally the Forestry Multifarm or the Ender IO Farming Station . To obtain seed oil, place these in a fluid extractor. Fish oil can be obtained from fish, which can be obtained in bulk from GT++ Fish Catchers or the GT++ Fishing Port multiblock.
Ethanol can be made from distilling forestry biomass (more efficient) or fermented biomass. These can be obtained by compressing plants into plantballs, making that into bio chaff, and putting the bio chaff into either a brewing machine, fluid canning machine, or pyrolyse oven (in order of efficiency) and fermenting, or by putting the bio chaff into a chemical bath to make mulch, and putting that into a brewing machine or pyrolyse oven. Methanol can be made from carbon monoxide or carbon monoxide plus hydrogen in a chemical reactor, or distilled from fermented biomass. It's less efficient than ethanol to make from biomass, but can be made from chemicals at MV. It is also possible to recycle methanol from glycerol which is a byproduct of producing bio diesel.
Sodium hydroxide can be made by distilling salt water, or by mixing sodium and water in a chemical reactor. It's the hardest to make renewable, since you need sodium or salt, but you only need small quantities of it (one dust can make 54 cells of bio diesel)
These 3 ingredients are then mixed together in a chemical reactor. From there, it can be burned directly or, once HV is reached, mixed with tetranitromethane(nitric acid and ethenone in a chemical reactor) to get cetane-boosted diesel.
Glycerol is a byproduct of producing bio diesel and can be used to make epoxid in EV for dynamite or electrolyzed into more carbon dust, hydrogen, and oxygen than is needed to recycle the methanol.
Used in: Combustion Generators
Benzene
Benzene is another renewable fuel, made from charcoal and wood tar in a pyrolyse oven and later in a ICO (Industrial Coke Oven). It is fairly simple to make, but requires several fluid extractors to run at max speed. It is first available at MV, requiring an MV distillery to obtain it from Wood Tar, and it gets significantly stronger in EV when ICO and multiblock turbines become available. Benzene (when upgraded to its enhanced version, Nitrobenzene) is viable until LuV+ (you can even use it all the way to UHV if you spam enough XL turbines, but with regular turbines you should plan to switch to fusion as soon as possible).
The first step is creating Wood Tar and Charcoal from wood. Using nitrogen recipe is highly suggested. Then send all the outgoing Charcoal to Fluid Extractors to be made into more Wood Tar, then send all of that into an MV Distillery to be made into Benzene. After having reached HV, the Distillery can be replaced with a Distillation Tower, which outputs Toluene, Phenol, Dimethylbenzene and Creosote Oil alongside the Benzene. The first two are good fuels as well, alongside being useful for other chemistry. Additionally, Toluene and Dimethylbenzene are a great source of carbon and hydrogen when electrolyzed, which is especially useful for producing Nitrobenzene.
Nitrobenzene is an upgrade from benzene and can be produced in a GT++ Chemical Plant (there is a recipe in the Large Chemical Reactor , but it should not be used for power production). In comparison to benzene it can be used in XL Gas turbines, making it a direct upgrade to benzene power when moving from regular gas turbines to XLGTs in LuV.
Used in: Gas turbines
Solar Panels
Solar panels are available in tiers from 1 EU/t all the way up to UV (524288 EU/t). Creating a solar panel of a given tier requires you to be 2 tiers higher than the panel (i.e. to make a LV panel you need to be HV). Solars are a viable power source from MV up to UV, but are never a main power source due to the tier requirement, however they can nicely help your regular power gen, especially in operations that need to be running all the time or far away from your main power source.
Production: Solars up to ULV are crafted in the regular crafting grid, then in the Solar Factory multiblock. Panels are quite expensive to make up for not needing fuel, especially more so if you're making them without the previous solar panel.
Usage: Solar panels can be placed as a cover on a GT machine, battery buffer, machine hull or even cable, or crafted into a standalone solar panel block. Cover-type solars need periodic cleaning by right-clicking with empty hand while having a bucket of water in your inventory (can be done by golems), or their output will decrease. Solar panel blocks lack this disadvantage, also you don't need to protect them from rain.
Thaumcraft offers an option to make compressed solar panels. These take 8 panels of the previous tier to produce 10 times more power, so even if recipes become exponentially more expensive there's a bit of advantage. Octuple compressed solar panels can produce 100,000,000 EU/t, which is almost 200 times more than a UV solar panel. Moreover, there are infused versions of compressed solars which produce even more power under certain conditions. For example, octuple aqua infused solar can produce up to 600,000,000 EU/t while in thunderstorm. These also have the added bonus of being very TPS efficient, which is very important late game.
Starting from triple onwards, it will require infusion. Read the Infusion automation guide for help on automating these solars. The maximum tier is 8 (Octuple), and requires 16777216 1 volt solars. This spreadsheet lists all items needed to create an UV Solar Panel and an Octuple Compressed Solar. The sheet is outdated for the former, since it was made before solar factory was added.
Magic Generators
Similar to Solar Panels are the Magic Energy Absorbers , which can generate power from LV to EV passively using energized nodes or a dragon egg placed on top of it. It is fairly expensive compared to non-passive EV generators, but considerably cheaper than EV solars, so it can be a good solution for powering multiblock miners, farms, etc in the midgame.
Magic Energy Converters consume various resources, and make up to one HV amp. They can power farms that produce those very resources, for example 4 Master Magic Energy Converters can supply 1 amp of EV power to an Extreme Entity Crusher that makes Forbidden Magic shards among other things.
Nuclear Reactors
See More: Nuclear Reactors
They're available starting in EV, and are VERY good. See the Nuclear Reactors page for details.
Large Heat Exchanger / WWXL / Extreme Heat Exchanger
See More: Large Heat Exchanger , Whakawhiti Wera XL , Extreme Heat Exchanger and Thermal Boiler
These multiblocks all produce steam by consuming some kind of hot liquid. They typically work as a middle step between Nuclear or Fusion Reactors and Steam Turbines to produce even more power at the cost of more processing steps. All Heat Exchangers blow up if not properly supplied with water or distilled water.
- Large Heat Exchanger consumes hot coolant, lava or solar salt (hot) to convert distilled water into steam or superheated steam. It also returns the cold version of respective coolant. For example, lava is converted into pahoehoe lava which can be centrifuged for some basic resources: copper, tin, silver, aluminium, phosphorus, titanium and tungsten (though not very much and requires quite a bit of power).
- Whakawhiti Wera XL acts like 32 Large Heat Exchangers in one and can process lava, hot coolant and, despite not being explicitly stated in the tooltip, Solar Salt (Hot) from a Solar Tower.
- Extreme Heat Exchanger can either act like basically 10 Large Heat Exchangers, but its main purpose is to create supercritical steam. It will only generate supercritical steam after reaching specified input threshold (does not apply to plasma which produces it regardless of amount supplied) and it is the only source of supercritical steam.
- Thermal Boiler can consume lava, pahoehoe lava or solar salt (hot) and makes either superheated or regular steam. It isn't known for high throughput rate but is quite cheap and can return small amounts of rare materials from lavas without centrifuging, among them: gold, silver, tantalum and tungstate.
Large Steam Turbines consume steam and return distilled water, Large HP Steam Turbines consume superheated steam and return steam, and Large SC Steam Turbines consume supercritical steam and also return steam.
Hot coolant basically comes from nukes (it can also come from Deep Earth Heating Pumps, Bees, and a few other sources, but these are all hilariously unviable).
Lava can be made from some bees or by pumping the nether, but in the quantities you need it, Everburn Urns or the Blood Magic Serenade of the Nether are preferred.
Plasma comes mainly from fusion reactors (there are some exceptions like Hydrogen Plasma from the Cyclotron but these are not really relevant for power gen).
The best plasmas to use for steam conversion are high power density ones, primarily those from the main Plasma line. Runite Plasma should be your first choice early on, switching to either Americium or Celestial Tungsten Plasma to power your setups in UHV and beyond.
Finally the solar salt (hot) comes from the Solar Tower. Its not a mainstream power source due to its high price in materials and relative setup complexity.
Kinetic Wind and Water Generators
See More: Kinetic Generators
Kinetic Wind and Water Generators from IC2 open up after the moon. They need Titanium and Platinum cables (and tons of other resources). You also need a Kinetic Gearbox Rotor. Here, many options are available from IC2 and GT++. Their main differences lie in cost, durability and the power output. The Iridium rotor from GT++ has the highest output and is also unbreakable, you will never have to replace it.
These generators don't produce EU directly, they generate KU, which needs to be fed into a Kinetic Generator. If you put in a rotor, you will see it appear on the side with the black dot, the Kinetic Generator goes onto the opposite side (black ring with silver dot). The Kinetic Generator itself is sided too, its side with the black dot needs to face the Wind or Water Generator. It will generate 1 EU/t for every 4 KU input. You can pull the power out using GT cables, but only 1A per side. With better rotors, a Kinetic Generator can produce more than 1A of its tier, so you have to pull power from more than one side to not waste anything. It is safe to connect cables of the generators tier, even when it produces more energy. The best height for Wind generators is at y-level 160, but you can use the Windmeter to check it yourself. Rotors can't overlap with other Kinetic Generators. Obviously, water turbines need to have submerged rotors and they only work in Ocean and River biomes. More information can be found on the IC2-wiki pages for Kinetic Wind Generator and Kinetic Water Generator .
Be careful, while IC2 machines don't mind the rain, your GT battery buffers and transformers will, so remember to build a roof above them.
The Kinetic Generators from IC2 output HV power . There are upgraded versions available from the Compact Kinetic Wind and Water Generators mod. So the Low generators are EV, Medium IV, High LuV and Extreme ZPM.
Enriched Naquadah/Naquadria Reactors
See More: Large Naquadah Reactor and Naquadah Fuel Refinery
Singleblock naquadah reactors produce large amounts of power at a constant eu/t, as stated on the machine's tooltip. These drain power depending by depleting tiberium/enriched naquadah/naquadria screw/rods/long rods into normal naquadah screws/rods/long rods, converting it into an internal buffer that is drained at a constant eu/t. The efficiency of the machine multiplies the EU potential of the rod, giving the true energy per item. They are best for remote mining drills and should not be used as a main source of power.
The Large Naquadah Reactor (LNR) is much different from the singleblock reactors. Instead of rods, it consumes nuclear based fuels for breeding and naquadah based fuels for power generation. There are six tiers of naquadah fuel: MK1 and MK2 fuels are made in a fusion reactor while MK3 and above are made in the Naquadah Fuel Refinery , a multiblock available late into UHV. The LNR requires liquid air to function and optionally can be supplied with o ne type of coolant and one type of booster to further improve power output. Coolants increase the efficiency of the naquadah based fuels (IC2 coolant: 105% efficiency, super coolant: 150% efficiency, Cryotheum: 275%, and Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid: 500%). Boosters increase both the fuel consumption and output of the reactor (molten caesium: 2x, molten U-235: 3x, molten naquadah: 4x, molten atomic separation catalyst: 16x, and spatially enlarged fluid: 64x).
The LNR is much better than plasma turbines because there is no turbine durability to worry about, higher power output, and less space required.
Fusion and Plasma
See More: Fusion Reactor
Fusion is unlocked in late LuV, opening the gate to ZPM and also to very powerful power generation. The Fusion Reactor is needed to create some new materials, but the plasma itself can give out a lot of EU if processed in the right machines. Not all the outputs of the reactor are plasmas, but the ones that are can all be used to generate power. Fusion reactors have unique 2/2 overclocks per tier.
The reactor itself needs a large, initial EU input to start working, and then needs additional energy while it processes the inputs into the outputs. If it ever stops, it will need the initial EU again to resume working. After getting it to work, the plasma can be moved into one of several machines. Plasma turbines convert it directly to EU and also output the molten version of the material that the plasma was made of. Large plasma turbine is available in LuV and XL plasma turbine is available in ZPM. Large plasma turbine does not accept tectech dynamo hatches while the XL one does. Instead of this, the EHE(Extreme Heat Exchanger) can also be used to generate supercritical steam from the plasma, adding another step to the process but tripling the fuel efficiency. While the EHE appears to be the superior option, it does not scale well, so it is only recommended to company regular fusion reactors and not compact fusion reactors.
Plasmas that are commonly used for power generation are helium and tin plasma. Helium plasma produces 2,560,000 EU/t on a MK3 reactor (before turbine and EHE efficiency) and is generally preferred due to the source materials (Helium-3 and Deterium) being easily obtainable. Tin plasma produces 5,480,928 EU/t on a MK3 reactor and has the advantage of higher energy output and higher energy density (which is proportional to the maximum processing capability of EHE).
Be warned that the XL Plasma Turbine does apply harsh penalties to plasmas with low energy density that run through good turbine blades.
Dyson Swarm
See More: Dyson Swarm Ground Unit
Eye of Harmony
See More: Eye of Harmony
Antimatter
